title.zh: 卷273 列傳六十 李率泰 赵廷臣 郎廷佐 佟凤彩 麻勒吉 施维翰
title.en: Volume 273 Biographies 60: Li Lvtai, Zhao Tingchen, Lang Tingzuo, Tong Feng Cai, Ma Leiji, Shi Weihan
title.raw: 卷273 列傳六十 李率泰 赵廷臣 郎廷佐 佟凤彩 麻勒吉 施维翰

sentences.zh: 列傳六十

translations.literal: Biographies 60
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 60

sentences.zh: 李率泰，字壽疇，漢軍正藍旗人，永芳子。

translations.literal: Li Lvtai—courtesy name Shouzhou—was a member of the Hanjun Plain Blue Banner and the son of Yongfang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lvtai, courtesy name Shouzhou, was of the Hanjun Plain Blue Banner and the son of Yongfang.

sentences.zh: 初名延齡，年十二，入侍太祖，賜今名。

translations.literal: His original name was Yanling; at the age of twelve he entered service to Taizu, who bestowed his present name.
translations.idiomatic: He was first called Yanling; at twelve he entered the Taizu's service and was granted his present name.

sentences.zh: 年十六，以宗室女妻之。

translations.literal: At sixteen, a woman of the imperial clan was given to him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he was married to a woman of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，從太宗徵察哈爾、朝鮮及明錦州，又從貝勒阿巴泰徵山東，並有功，洊擢梅勒額真。

translations.literal: Upon reaching manhood he followed Taizong in campaigns against the Chahar, Korea, and Ming Jinzhou, and again followed Prince Abatai against Shandong; in all he rendered merit and was repeatedly promoted to Meirei Ejen.
translations.idiomatic: Coming of age, he followed Taizong against the Chahar, Korea, and Ming Jinzhou, and later Prince Abatai into Shandong; each time he distinguished himself, and he rose repeatedly to Meirei Ejen.

sentences.zh: 順治元年，命以刑部參政兼任，率師駐防錦州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi he was ordered to serve concurrently as a canjun of the Board of Punishments and to lead troops garrisoning Jinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 1 he was ordered to hold a concurrent post as vice minister of the Board of Punishments and to lead troops garrisoning Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 四月，從睿親王多爾袞入關，破李自成；

translations.literal: In the fourth month he followed Prince Regent Dorgon through the passes and defeated Li Zicheng;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he followed Prince Regent Dorgon through the passes and routed Li Zicheng;

sentences.zh: 又率兵徇山東、河南，斬自成將趙應元，降其眾萬人。

translations.literal: he also led troops through Shandong and Henan, beheaded Zicheng's general Zhao Yingyuan, and received the surrender of ten thousand of his men.
translations.idiomatic: then led troops through Shandong and Henan, killed Zicheng's general Zhao Yingyuan, and accepted the surrender of ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 二年，從豫親王多鐸破自成兵潼關。

translations.literal: In the second year he followed Prince Dodo and broke Zicheng's army at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 he followed Prince Dodo and shattered Zicheng's forces at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 移師南征，克揚州，下江寧，分兵定蘇州、松江諸郡。

translations.literal: The army shifted south, took Yangzhou, captured Jiangning, and detached forces to secure Suzhou, Songjiang, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The army marched south, took Yangzhou, captured Jiangning, and sent detachments to secure Suzhou, Songjiang, and the surrounding prefectures.

sentences.zh: 江陰典史閻應元拒守，督兵攻破之。

translations.literal: Yan Yingyuan, the diantai of Jiangyin, held out in defense; Lvtai directed troops and stormed the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Yingyuan, diantai of Jiangyin, held the city against him; he directed the assault and took it.

sentences.zh: 豫親王令駐防蘇州。

translations.literal: Prince Dodo ordered him to garrison Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dodo ordered him to garrison Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 會明將吳志葵、黃蜚等來犯，時城兵僅千餘，率泰使繞城張幟為援兵狀。

translations.literal: When Ming generals Wu Zhigui, Huang Fei, and others attacked, the garrison had barely a thousand men; Lvtai had banners raised around the walls to simulate reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming generals Wu Zhigui, Huang Fei, and others attacked, the city held barely a thousand troops; Lvtai had banners posted around the walls to look like relief forces.

sentences.zh: 志葵等斬關入，勁騎突起截擊，盡殲之。

translations.literal: Zhigui and the rest cut through the gate and entered; fierce cavalry sprang out and intercepted them, annihilating them all.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigui and his men forced the gate and entered; then crack cavalry burst out and cut them off, wiping them out to the last man.

sentences.zh: 三年，從端重親王博洛平浙江、福建，敘功，授世職二等阿達哈哈番兼拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: In the third year he followed Prince Duanzhong Bolo in pacifying Zhejiang and Fujian; for his merit he was granted the hereditary ranks of second-class adaha gūsa with tashala gūsa.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3 he followed Prince Duanzhong Bolo in pacifying Zhejiang and Fujian; for his service he received the hereditary ranks of second-class adaha gūsa and tashala gūsa.

sentences.zh: 五年，鄭彩犯福建漳、泉諸郡，詔率泰與靖南將軍陳泰協剿，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Zheng Cai invaded the Zhang and Quan prefectures of Fujian; an edict ordered Lvtai and the Jingnan General Chen Tai to join in suppression, and they beheaded and captured a great many.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 5 Zheng Cai raided the Zhang and Quan districts of Fujian; the court ordered Lvtai and Jingnan General Chen Tai to suppress him jointly, and they killed and captured in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 复長樂、連江二縣。

translations.literal: They recovered the two counties of Changle and Lianjiang.
translations.idiomatic: They recovered Changle and Lianjiang.

sentences.zh: 彩走，复擒斬所署總督顧世臣等，遂克興化。

translations.literal: Cai fled; they again captured and beheaded his appointed governor Gu Shichen and others, and then took Xinghua.
translations.idiomatic: Cai fled; they captured and executed his appointed governor Gu Shichen and others, then took Xinghua.

sentences.zh: 寇攻福州十四月，圍始解。

translations.literal: The rebels besieged Fuzhou for fourteen months before the siege was finally lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels had besieged Fuzhou for fourteen months before the blockade was finally broken.

sentences.zh: 民食盡，江西盜郭天才自杉關長驅至福州，載米麥江上，誘民出就食。

translations.literal: The people's food was exhausted; the Jiangxi bandit Guo Tiancai marched from Shan Pass straight to Fuzhou, loaded rice and wheat on boats on the river, and lured the people out to obtain food.
translations.idiomatic: With food exhausted, the Jiangxi bandit Guo Tiancai marched from Shan Pass to Fuzhou, loaded grain onto boats on the river, and lured people out to be fed.

sentences.zh: 率泰師次建寧，檄守吏嚴備，乃夜焚洪山橋遁。

translations.literal: Lvtai's army halted at Jianning; he issued orders to the defending officials to make strict preparations, and at night Guo burned Hongshan Bridge and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Lvtai halted at Jianning and ordered the local defenders to stand ready; Guo burned Hongshan Bridge that night and fled.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史周世科虐刑婪賄，率泰疏劾，置諸法。

translations.literal: The touring censor Zhou Shike inflicted cruel punishments and took bribes greedily; Lvtai memorialized impeaching him, and he was punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Touring censor Zhou Shike tortured prisoners and took bribes; Lvtai impeached him by memorial, and he was punished under the law.

sentences.zh: 六年，從征大同叛將薑瓖，下保德州，擒瓖黨牛化麟等。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed the campaign against the Datong rebel Jiang Xiang, took Baode Prefecture, and captured Xiang's partisans Niu Hualin and others.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 6 he joined the campaign against the Datong rebel Jiang Xiang, took Baode, and captured Xiang's followers Niu Hualin and others.

sentences.zh: 敘功，復加拖沙喇哈番。

translations.literal: For his merit he was again granted tashala gūsa.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he received an additional tashala gūsa rank.

sentences.zh: 初定官制，改參政為侍郎，率泰仍以刑部侍郎兼梅勒額真。

translations.literal: When the official system was first fixed, canjun was changed to vice minister; Lvtai still held the post of vice minister of the Board of Punishments concurrently with Meirei Ejen.
translations.idiomatic: When the bureaucracy was first regularized, canjun posts became vice ministries; Lvtai remained vice minister of the Board of Punishments while also holding Meirei Ejen.

sentences.zh: 八年，調吏部，拜弘文院大學士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to the Board of Personnel and appointed Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 8 he moved to the Board of Personnel and was made a Grand Secretary of the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 條奏請懲貪酷官吏，給滿洲兵馬草料，酌量營造工程次第，上從之。

translations.literal: He submitted detailed memorials requesting punishment of greedy and cruel officials, provision of fodder for Manchu troops and horses, and measured ordering of construction projects; the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized in detail for punishing corrupt and cruel officials, supplying fodder for Manchu troops and horses, and sequencing public works by priority; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 未幾，與大學士陳泰坐誤增恩詔赦款，並罷任，降世職為拜他喇布勒哈番。

translations.literal: Before long, he and Grand Secretary Chen Tai were dismissed for erroneously expanding the amnesty clauses of an imperial grace edict; both lost their posts, and his hereditary rank was reduced to baitalabuleha gūsa.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he and Grand Secretary Chen Tai were dismissed for wrongly expanding an amnesty edict; both lost office, and his hereditary rank was cut to baitalabuleha gūsa.

sentences.zh: 九年，特進三等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was specially advanced to third-class ashan-iha gūsa.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 9 he was specially promoted to third-class ashan-iha gūsa.

sentences.zh: 十年，用大學士洪承疇薦，授兩廣總督。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, on the recommendation of Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou, he was appointed governor-general of Guangdong and Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 10, on Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou's recommendation, he was made governor-general of the Two Guangs.

sentences.zh: 時明桂王硃由榔居安隆，其將李定國擁兵廣西，土寇廖篤增等應之。

translations.literal: At that time the Ming Prince of Gui Zhu Youlang dwelt at Anlong; his general Li Dingguo held troops in Guangxi, and local bandits such as Liao Duzeng responded to them.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Prince of Gui, Zhu Youlang, was at Anlong; his general Li Dingguo held Guangxi with an army, and local bandits such as Liao Duzeng rallied to them.

sentences.zh: 十一年，率泰遣兵進剿，斬篤增於玉版巢。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Lvtai sent troops on a suppression campaign and beheaded Duzeng at Yuban Nest.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 11 Lvtai sent troops against them and killed Duzeng at Yuban Nest.

sentences.zh: 十二年，定國犯廣東，率泰御之，敗其將高文貴。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Dingguo invaded Guangdong; Lvtai resisted him and defeated his general Gao Wengui.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 12 Dingguo invaded Guangdong; Lvtai met him and defeated his general Gao Wengui.

sentences.zh: 會靖南將軍珠瑪喇率禁旅至，合兵夾擊，大破之。

translations.literal: When Jingnan General Zhumala arrived leading the Forbidden Troops, they joined forces in a pincer attack and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Jingnan General Zhumala then arrived with the Forbidden Troops; the two armies struck from both sides and routed Dingguo utterly.

sentences.zh: 復高、雷二郡。

translations.literal: They recovered the two prefectures of Gao and Lei.
translations.idiomatic: They recovered Gao and Lei.

sentences.zh: 十三年，加太子太保，調閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and transferred to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 13 he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and transferred to governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 率泰有方略，善用兵，與士卒同甘苦。

translations.literal: Lvtai had strategy and was skilled in using troops, sharing hardship and comfort with his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Lvtai was resourceful and skilled in command, sharing hardship and comfort with his men.

sentences.zh: 時鄭成功據台灣，數入寇。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Chenggong held Taiwan and repeatedly raided inward.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Chenggong held Taiwan and raided the coast again and again.

sentences.zh: 率泰疏請增設水師三千，造哨船百餘艘，招降海盜，散其羽翼。

translations.literal: Lvtai memorialized requesting an additional three thousand naval troops, construction of more than a hundred patrol vessels, and recruitment of surrendered pirates to break up his support.
translations.idiomatic: Lvtai asked to add three thousand naval troops, build more than a hundred patrol craft, and win over pirates to strip Chenggong of his allies.

sentences.zh: 又言成功父芝龍不宜徙寧古塔，其地近海，恐乘間遁歸，為患滋大。

translations.literal: He also said that Chenggong's father Zhilong ought not to be moved to Ningguta, for that place was near the sea and he feared Zhilong might seize an opportunity to escape and return, making the trouble even greater.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that Chenggong's father Zhilong should not be sent to Ningguta: the place lay near the sea, and Zhilong might slip away and return to make matters worse.

sentences.zh: 世祖悉用其言。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor adopted all his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizu Emperor adopted every point.

sentences.zh: 以破定國功，進世職一等。

translations.literal: For the merit of defeating Dingguo, his hereditary rank was advanced to first class.
translations.idiomatic: For defeating Dingguo his hereditary rank was raised to first class.

sentences.zh: 考滿，加少保。

translations.literal: Upon completion of his performance review he was given the additional title Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of his term review he was made Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 十五年，招撫成功將唐邦傑、林翀、葉祿等，降者數万人。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he recruited and pacified Chenggong's generals Tang Bangjie, Lin Chong, Ye Lu, and others; those who surrendered numbered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 15 he won over Chenggong's generals Tang Bangjie, Lin Chong, Ye Lu, and others; tens of thousands surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十五年，成功攻溫州，陷平陽、瑞安，率泰調江寧滿洲兵助剿，成功敗走。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Chenggong attacked Wenzhou, took Pingyang and Ruian; Lvtai mobilized the Manchu troops of Jiangning to assist in suppression, and Chenggong was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Chenggong struck Wenzhou and took Pingyang and Ruian; Lvtai called up the Jiangning Manchu garrison, Chenggong was beaten, and fled.

sentences.zh: 是年，詔分閩浙總督為二：以都統​​趙國祚督浙江，駐溫州；

translations.literal: That year an edict divided the Fujian-Zhejiang governor-generalship in two: the dutong Zhao Guozuo was to supervise Zhejiang, stationed at Wenzhou;
translations.idiomatic: That year the court split the Fujian-Zhejiang post: dutong Zhao Guozuo took Zhejiang and was stationed at Wenzhou;

sentences.zh: 而以率泰專督福建，駐福州。

translations.literal: while Lvtai was to supervise Fujian alone, stationed at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lvtai alone governed Fujian from Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，成功據南安嶺窺福州，其黨陳斌既降复叛，率眾據羅星塔。

translations.literal: Before long Chenggong held Nan'an Ridge and watched for an opening against Fuzhou; his partisan Chen Bin had surrendered and then rebelled again, leading troops to hold Luoxing Pagoda.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chenggong held Nan'an Ridge and menaced Fuzhou; his follower Chen Bin had surrendered, rebelled again, and seized Luoxing Pagoda with a force.

sentences.zh: 率泰檄兵燔其巨艦千餘，成功遁。

translations.literal: Lvtai ordered troops to burn more than a thousand of his great ships; Chenggong fled.
translations.idiomatic: Lvtai sent troops to burn more than a thousand of his great junks; Chenggong fled.

sentences.zh: 斌复降，奏誅之。

translations.literal: Bin surrendered again; Lvtai memorialized requesting his execution.
translations.idiomatic: Bin surrendered again; Lvtai memorialized for his execution.

sentences.zh: 十六年，坐事奪世職，任總督如故。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, for an offense he was stripped of his hereditary rank but continued in the governor-general post as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 16 he lost his hereditary rank for an offense but kept the governorship.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，率泰以漳州為福建門戶，奏增設水師二千。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, Lvtai, holding that Zhangzhou was Fujian's gateway, memorialized to add two thousand naval troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 Lvtai argued that Zhangzhou was Fujian's gateway and asked for two thousand more naval troops.

sentences.zh: 尋與靖南王耿繼茂擊走定海小埕諸寇，復與提督馬得功平萬安所，擊走成功將楊宣。

translations.literal: Soon he and Prince Jingnan Geng Jimao drove off the bandits of Dinghai Xiaocheng and others; again with Provincial Military Commissioner Ma Degong he pacified Wan'an Garrison and drove off Chenggong's general Yang Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he and Prince Jingnan Geng Jimao drove bandits from Dinghai Xiaocheng; with Provincial Military Commissioner Ma Degong he pacified Wan'an Garrison and routed Chenggong's general Yang Xuan.

sentences.zh: 是年成功死，其子錦拒命如故，部下漸攜貳。

translations.literal: That year Chenggong died; his son Jing still defied orders as before, and his subordinates gradually became divided in loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: That year Chenggong died; his son Jing still held out, and his followers began to waver.

sentences.zh: 於是率泰复招降其將林俊奇、陳輝、何義、魏明等三百餘人，兵二千有奇。

translations.literal: Thereupon Lvtai again recruited and received the surrender of his generals Lin Junqi, Chen Hui, He Yi, Wei Ming, and more than three hundred others, with somewhat more than two thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Lvtai then won over his generals Lin Junqi, Chen Hui, He Yi, Wei Ming, and more than three hundred others, along with somewhat over two thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 統建寧、延平、邵武三路士卒剿內地山寇，獲其渠王鐵佛，斬之。

translations.literal: He commanded troops of the three routes of Jianning, Yanping, and Shaowu to suppress mountain bandits in the interior, captured their leader Wang Tiefo, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops from the Jianning, Yanping, and Shaowu circuits against interior mountain bandits, captured their chief Wang Tiefo, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 既，錦率其將周全斌以五百餘人自梁山內犯，率泰遣總兵王進加、參將折光秋夾擊，大破之；

translations.literal: Afterward Jing led his general Zhou Quanbin with more than five hundred men to invade from within at Liangshan; Lvtai sent Regional Commander Wang Jinjia and Assistant Regional Commander Zhe Guangqiu to strike from both sides and inflicted a great defeat;
translations.idiomatic: Later Jing sent his general Zhou Quanbin with five hundred men inland from Liangshan; Lvtai sent Regional Commander Wang Jinjia and Assistant Regional Commander Zhe Guangqiu to hit them from both sides and routed them;

sentences.zh: 復與靖南王耿繼茂統舟師搗廈門，取浯嶼、金門二島，錦宵遁。

translations.literal: again he joined Prince Jingnan Geng Jimao in commanding the fleet to strike at Xiamen, took the two islands of Wuyu and Jinmen, and Jing fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: then he and Prince Jingnan Geng Jimao led the fleet against Xiamen, took Wuyu and Jinmen, and Jing fled by night.

sentences.zh: 三年，降其將林國梁，進兵八尺門，降其將翁求多；

translations.literal: In the third year he received the surrender of his general Lin Guoliang, advanced troops to Bachi Gate, and received the surrender of his general Weng Qiuduo;
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 3 he took the surrender of Lin Guoliang, advanced to Bachi Gate, and won over Weng Qiuduo;

sentences.zh: 夜半渡海拔銅山，斬級三千有奇，其將黃廷等率兵民三萬餘人來降，獲敵艦、軍械無算。

translations.literal: at midnight he crossed the sea by land route and took Tongshan, beheading more than three thousand; his general Huang Ting and others led more than thirty thousand soldiers and civilians to surrender, and captured enemy vessels and military equipment beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: at midnight his force crossed to Tongshan by land, killed more than three thousand, and Huang Ting and others brought over thirty thousand soldiers and civilians; enemy ships and arms were captured beyond count.

sentences.zh: 錦僅以數十艘遁入台灣。

translations.literal: Jing escaped into Taiwan with only several dozen vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Jing escaped to Taiwan with only a few dozen ships.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加秩正一品。

translations.literal: For his merit his rank was raised to the first grade.
translations.idiomatic: For his service his rank was raised to first grade.

sentences.zh: 尋以病累疏乞休，詔輒慰留。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of illness he repeatedly memorialized requesting retirement; each time an edict comforted him and kept him in post.
translations.idiomatic: Soon illness drove him to ask repeatedly to retire; each time the throne refused and urged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 5 he died in office.

sentences.zh: 遺疏言：「海賊遠竄台灣，奉旨撤兵，與民休息。

translations.literal: His final memorial said: "The sea rebels have fled far to Taiwan; by imperial order troops are to be withdrawn so the people may rest.
translations.idiomatic: His deathbed memorial read: "The sea rebels have fled to Taiwan; by imperial order the troops are to be withdrawn so the people may rest.

sentences.zh: 第將眾兵繁，撤之驟，易致驚疑；

translations.literal: Yet the forces are numerous; if withdrawal is too sudden, it may easily cause alarm and suspicion;
translations.idiomatic: But the armies are large; a sudden pullout may alarm them;

sentences.zh: 遲，又恐貽患。

translations.literal: if delayed, I fear it may leave trouble behind.
translations.idiomatic: delay, and trouble may linger.

sentences.zh: 今當安反側之心，後須防難制之勢。

translations.literal: For now we should settle hearts that waver; afterward we must guard against situations hard to control.
translations.idiomatic: For now hearts must be steadied; later we must guard against what cannot easily be controlled.

sentences.zh: 紅毛夾板船雖已回國，然往來頻仍，異時恐生釁。

translations.literal: The Dutch fluyts have returned to their country, yet they come and go frequently; in time to come I fear trouble may arise.
translations.idiomatic: The Dutch fluyts have gone home, yet they still come and go often; trouble may arise in time.

sentences.zh: 至數年以來，令沿海居民遷移內地，失其故業。

translations.literal: As for these several years past, coastal inhabitants have been ordered to move inland and have lost their former livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: For years now coastal people have been moved inland and have lost their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 宜略寬界限，俾獲耕漁，庶甦殘喘。」

translations.literal: The boundary restrictions ought to be somewhat relaxed so they may farm and fish, that the survivors may revive."
translations.idiomatic: The boundary ought to be eased a little so they can farm and fish again and the survivors breathe easier."

sentences.zh: 上聞，優詔褒卹，贈兵部尚書，复世職，諡忠襄。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this, he issued a gracious edict of praise and condolence, posthumously granted Minister of War, restored his hereditary rank, and gave the posthumous title Zhongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard it and issued a gracious edict of praise and mourning gifts, posthumously made him Minister of War, restored his hereditary rank, and gave him the posthumous title Zhongxiang.

sentences.zh: 趙廷臣，字君鄰，漢軍鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Zhao Tingchen—courtesy name Junlin—was a member of the Hanjun Bordered Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tingchen, courtesy name Junlin, was of the Hanjun Bordered Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 順治二年，自貢生授江蘇山陽知縣，遷江寧同知，有政聲。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shunzhi, from tribute student he was appointed magistrate of Shanyang in Jiangsu, was transferred to subprefect of Jiangning, and had a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 2 he entered office from the tribute student quota as magistrate of Shanyang in Jiangsu, became subprefect of Jiangning, and earned a name for good government.

sentences.zh: 坐催徵逾限，免。

translations.literal: For exceeding the time limit in tax collection he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed for collecting taxes past the deadline.

sentences.zh: 十年，大學士洪承疇經略湖廣，薦廷臣清幹，題授下湖南道副使，屢平冤獄。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou was grand coordinator of Huguang and recommended Tingchen for integrity and ability; he was nominated and appointed vice commissioner of the Lower Hunan Circuit, and repeatedly righted wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 10 Grand Secretary Hong Chengchou, coordinating Huguang, recommended Tingchen as upright and capable; he was appointed vice commissioner of the Lower Hunan Circuit and repeatedly cleared wrongful cases.

sentences.zh: 十三年，調督糧道。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was transferred to grain transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 13 he was made grain transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十五年，從定貴州，遂擢授巡撫。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he followed in pacifying Guizhou and was thereupon promoted and appointed provincial governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 15 he took part in pacifying Guizhou and was promoted to provincial governor.

sentences.zh: 甫至官，察民間疾苦，定賦蠲賑，懲貪橫，禁吏卒驛騷。

translations.literal: As soon as he reached his post he examined the people's hardships, fixed tax assessments and granted relief, punished the greedy and overbearing, and forbade clerks and runners from harassing the courier stations.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he took office he looked into popular hardship, set taxes and granted relief, punished the greedy and brutal, and stopped clerks and runners from harassing the post stations.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「貴州古稱鬼方，自城市外，四顧皆苗。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Guizhou was anciently called Guifang; beyond the cities, on all sides one looks upon Miao.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Guizhou was anciently called Guifang; beyond the cities, Miao are everywhere.

sentences.zh: 其貴陽以東，苗為夥，而銅苗、九股為悍；

translations.literal: East of Guiyang the Miao are numerous, and the Tong Miao and Jiugu are fierce;
translations.idiomatic: East of Guiyang the Miao are numerous; the Tong Miao and Jiugu are the fiercest;

sentences.zh: 其次為革老，曰羊黃，曰八番子，曰土人，曰侗人，曰蠻人，曰冉家蠻，皆黔東苗屬也。

translations.literal: next come the Gelao, called Yanghuang, called Bafanzi, called Turen, called Dongren, called Manren, called Ranjia Man—all belonging to the eastern Guizhou Miao.
translations.idiomatic: then the Gelao, Yanghuang, Bafanzi, Turen, Dong, Man, and Ranjia Man—all eastern Guizhou Miao groups.

sentences.zh: 自貴陽以西，羅羅為夥，而黑羅為悍；

translations.literal: West of Guiyang the Luoluo are numerous, and the Heiluo are fierce;
translations.idiomatic: West of Guiyang the Luoluo are numerous; the Heiluo are the fiercest;

sentences.zh: 其次曰仲家，曰米家，曰蔡家，曰龍家，曰白羅，皆黔西苗屬也。

translations.literal: next come the Zhongjia, Mijia, Caijia, Longjia, and Bailuo—all belonging to the western Guizhou Miao.
translations.idiomatic: then the Zhongjia, Mijia, Caijia, Longjia, and Bailuo—all western Guizhou Miao groups.

sentences.zh: 專事鬥殺，馭之甚難。

translations.literal: They devote themselves to fighting and killing; governing them is very difficult.
translations.idiomatic: They live by feud and bloodshed; they are hard to govern.

sentences.zh: 臣以為教化無不可施之地。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that there is no place where civilizing instruction cannot be applied.
translations.idiomatic: I believe civilization can reach anywhere.

sentences.zh: 請自後應襲土官年十三以上者，令入學習禮，由儒學起送承襲。

translations.literal: I request that hereafter native officials due to inherit at age thirteen and above be ordered to enter schools to study ritual, and be forwarded by the Confucian schools for succession.
translations.idiomatic: Let every native official heir aged thirteen or above study ritual in school and be forwarded by the county schools for succession.

sentences.zh: 其族屬子弟原入學讀書者，亦許其仕進，則儒教日興而悍俗漸變。

translations.literal: Clansmen and younger relatives who were already enrolled to study should also be permitted to advance in office; then Confucian teaching would daily flourish and fierce customs would gradually change.
translations.idiomatic: Let clansmen already in school also take office; then learning will spread and fierce customs will soften.

sentences.zh: 土官私襲，支係不明，爭奪易起，釀成變亂，令歲終錄其世次籍上布政司達部。

translations.literal: When native officials succeed privately, branch lines are unclear and struggles for succession easily arise, brewing into rebellion; I order that at year's end their genealogical registers be recorded and sent up through the provincial administration commission to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Private succession breeds unclear lines and fights for office that turn into revolt; require yearly genealogical registers sent through the provincial administration commission to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 有爭襲者，按籍立辨，豫杜釁端。」

translations.literal: When there are disputes over succession, decide according to the registers and forestall trouble at the outset."
translations.idiomatic: Disputes can be settled from the registers and trouble stopped before it starts."

sentences.zh: 並下部議行。

translations.literal: All was referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was sent to the ministries for implementation.

sentences.zh: 十六年，擢雲貴總督。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was promoted to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 16 he was made governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 土寇馮天裕陷湄潭，犯甕安，調兵擊卻之。

translations.literal: The native bandit Feng Tianyu took Meitan and invaded Weng'an; he mobilized troops and drove him back.
translations.idiomatic: The native bandit Feng Tianyu took Meitan and raided Weng'an; he sent troops and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 疏請改馬乃、曹滴諸土司為流官。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting that the native offices of Manai, Caodi, and others be changed to regular officials.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to replace the Manai, Caodi, and other native offices with regular officials.

sentences.zh: 又言：「貴州曩被寇，改衛為府，改所為縣，法令紛更，民苦重役，今應復舊制。

translations.literal: He also said: "Guizhou was formerly ravaged by rebels; guards were changed to prefectures and battalions to counties, laws and orders changed back and forth, and the people suffered heavy corvée; now the old system should be restored.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "After earlier raids, Guizhou's guards became prefectures and battalions became counties; laws kept changing and the people bore heavy labor; the old system should be restored.

sentences.zh: 雲南田土荒蕪，當招民開墾。

translations.literal: Yunnan's fields lie waste and overgrown; the people should be recruited to open and cultivate them.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan's fields lie fallow; settlers should be recruited to open them.

sentences.zh: 衝路州縣，請以順治十七年秋糧貸為春種資。」

translations.literal: For prefectures and counties on the main routes, I request that the autumn grain tax of Shunzhi 17 be lent as capital for spring planting."
translations.idiomatic: For counties on the main routes, lend the Shunzhi 17 autumn tax as seed grain for spring planting."

sentences.zh: 並下部議行。

translations.literal: All was referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: That too was sent to the ministries for implementation.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂貢象五，世祖命免送京，廷臣因乞概停邊貢，允之。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui presented five elephants in tribute; the Shizu Emperor ordered that they need not be sent to the capital; Tingchen thereupon requested a general halt to border tributes, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui sent five elephants as tribute; the Shizu Emperor waived sending them to the capital; Tingchen then asked to stop border tribute altogether, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十八年，以平土酋龍吉兆功，加兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, for the merit of pacifying the native chieftain Long Jizhao, he was given the additional title Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 18, for pacifying the native chieftain Long Jizhao, he was made Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 是年調浙江。

translations.literal: That year he was transferred to Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was transferred to Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 敘雲南墾荒勞，加太子少保。

translations.literal: For his labor in opening wasteland in Yunnan he was given the additional title Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: For opening wasteland in Yunnan he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，疏言：「浙江逋賦不清，由徵解繁雜，請以一條鞭法令各州縣隨徵隨解，布政司察明註冊，至為簡易。」

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi he memorialized: "Zhejiang's arrears in tax payment are unclear because collection and forwarding are complicated; I request that the single-whip law order each prefecture and county to collect and forward as they go, with the provincial administration commission examining and registering clearly—this would be simplest."
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 2 he wrote: "Zhejiang's tax arrears stay unclear because collection and forwarding are tangled; let the single-whip law require each county to collect and remit at once, with the provincial administration commission keeping clear registers—that would be simplest."

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「徵糧之法不一，苟能寓撫字於催科，即百姓受其福。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Methods of grain tax collection are not uniform; if one can embody nurturing care within collection, the common people will receive the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Grain-tax methods differ everywhere; if collectors can show care even while pressing payment, the people benefit.

sentences.zh: 急公好義，人情皆然。

translations.literal: Eagerness for public duty and love of righteousness—human feeling is the same for all.
translations.idiomatic: People will pay willingly when treated fairly—that is human nature.

sentences.zh: 有​​司止以箠楚為能，民安得不重利借債，減價賣產？

translations.literal: Officials take beating with rods as their only skill—how can the people avoid borrowing at heavy interest and selling property at reduced prices?
translations.idiomatic: When officials know only the whip, people borrow at ruinous rates and sell land cheap.

sentences.zh: 錢糧完，地方壞矣。

translations.literal: When money and grain taxes are complete, the locality is ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The treasury may be full while the countryside is ruined.

sentences.zh: 苟能得廉有司，禁革火耗，天平不欺天，法馬不違法，又禁絕差擾，一酒一飯無不為民節省，民未有不交納恐後者。

translations.literal: If one can obtain upright officials, forbid and abolish surcharges for melting fees, keep scales honest before heaven and standard weights lawful, and also forbid entirely runner harassment—saving the people even a cup of wine or a meal—there has never been a people who did not pay taxes for fear of being last.
translations.idiomatic: With honest officials who end surcharges, keep honest scales and weights, and stop runner harassment—saving the people even a cup of wine or a meal—people will rush to pay.

sentences.zh: 徵糧之能，在人不在法，然不得其人而循法行之，亦得半之道也。

translations.literal: The ability to collect grain taxes lies in men, not in laws; yet if one cannot obtain the right men but follows the law in practice, one still gains half the way.
translations.idiomatic: Good collection depends on people, not rules alone—but even following the rules without the right men gets you halfway.

sentences.zh: 實徵冊籍立實在戶名，以杜詭卸；

translations.literal: Actual collection registers should list real household names to stop fraudulent shifting of liability;
translations.idiomatic: Registers should list real household names to stop shifting liability;

sentences.zh: 流水紅簿送本府印發，以防侵蝕；

translations.literal: running-account red registers should be sent to the prefecture for sealing and issuance to prevent embezzlement;
translations.idiomatic: running-account ledgers should be sealed at the prefecture to prevent embezzlement;

sentences.zh: 易知由單遍散窮山深谷，以絕橫索。

translations.literal: simple notice slips should be distributed throughout remote mountains and deep valleys to end extortionate demands.
translations.idiomatic: payment notices should reach remote valleys so extortion ends.

sentences.zh: 臣於浙屬立法通行，催徵得法之吏，請敕部酌議，許題請獎勵。」

translations.literal: Your subject has enacted these laws throughout Zhejiang subordinates; for collectors who obtain grain by proper methods, I request that the ministry deliberate and permit nomination for reward."
translations.idiomatic: I have put these rules into practice in Zhejiang; let the ministry allow rewards for collectors who follow them."

sentences.zh: 又疏請移海島投誠官兵分插內地，杜其煽誘；

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting that surrendered officers and troops from the sea islands be moved inland in separate postings to cut off their incitement and enticement;
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to resettle surrendered island troops inland in separate postings to stop them stirring trouble;

sentences.zh: 定水師提鎮各營兵制，以備水戰。

translations.literal: fix the troop establishments of each naval camp under the provincial admiral and regional commanders to prepare for naval combat.
translations.idiomatic: and fix naval camp establishments for war at sea.

sentences.zh: 杭、嘉、湖三郡毗連太湖，易藏奸宄，請增造快號船，撥兵巡哨。

translations.literal: The three prefectures of Hang, Jia, and Hu border Lake Tai and easily hide traitors and villains; I request additional construction of fast patrol boats and allocation of troops for cruising patrol.
translations.idiomatic: Hang, Jia, and Hu border Lake Tai and hide trouble easily; build more fast patrol boats and assign cruising troops.

sentences.zh: 詔並從之。

translations.literal: Edicts approved all in each case.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved all of it.

sentences.zh: 時鄭成功死，廷臣招明魯王所署將軍阮美、都督鄭殷、侍郎蔡昌登等，皆率眾來降；

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Chenggong had died; Tingchen recruited the Ming Prince of Lu's appointed General Ruan Mei, Commander Zheng Yin, Vice Minister Cai Changdeng, and others, all of whom led their followers to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong had just died; Tingchen won over the Ming Prince of Lu's appointees General Ruan Mei, Commander Zheng Yin, Vice Minister Cai Changdeng, and others, who all came over with their men;

sentences.zh: 惟張煌言散兵居定海山中，執而殺之。

translations.literal: only Zhang Huangyan, with scattered troops dwelling in the mountains of Dinghai, was seized and killed.
translations.idiomatic: only Zhang Huangyan, with scattered men in the Dinghai hills, was captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 四年，疏請崇節儉，維風俗。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he memorialized requesting promotion of frugality and preservation of custom.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 4 he asked the court to promote frugality and shore up public morals.

sentences.zh: 又言用人宜寬小眚，請敕部分別罣誤降革人員，量才錄用。

translations.literal: He also said that in employing men one should be lenient toward minor faults, and requested an edict to the ministries to distinguish personnel demoted or dismissed for entanglement in error and employ them according to ability.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged leniency for minor faults and asked the ministries to review wrongly demoted men and employ them by merit.

sentences.zh: 又言民人鬻身旗下，宜令有司給與印契，並曉諭鄰里，後或逃歸，有容留者，乃可坐以窩逃。

translations.literal: He also said that when common people sell themselves into banner households, the local officials should issue sealed contracts and also instruct the neighbors; if afterward they flee back and someone harbors them, only then may one punish for sheltering fugitives.
translations.idiomatic: He also said people sold into banner households should receive sealed contracts from local officials and notice to neighbors; only then could harboring a runaway be punished.

sentences.zh: 並議行。

translations.literal: All were deliberated and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved for implementation.

sentences.zh: 時錢滯不行，疏請令外省收銅開鑄，準寶泉、寶源兩局法式，去各省分鑄之名，以天下之錢供天下之用。

translations.literal: At that time cash did not circulate; he memorialized requesting that outer provinces collect copper and open mints, following the standards of the two Baoquan and Baoyuan bureaus, abolishing the names of separate provincial minting, so that the empire's coin would supply the empire's use.
translations.idiomatic: Cash was scarce; he asked outer provinces to gather copper and mint coin to Baoquan and Baoyuan standards, ending separate provincial mint names so one coin supply served the realm.

sentences.zh: 上命复各省二十四監鑄錢。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered restoration of the twenty-four provincial mints to cast coin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instead restored the twenty-four provincial mints.

sentences.zh: 浙東初平，叛獄屢起，廷臣平情讞鞫，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Eastern Zhejiang had just been pacified and rebel cases arose repeatedly; Tingchen judged cases with equanimity and spared a great many lives.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Zhejiang had only just been pacified and rebel trials piled up; Tingchen judged fairly and spared many lives.

sentences.zh: 時海濱尚多餘孽，聞廷臣寬大，多解甲來歸。

translations.literal: At that time many remnants still remained along the coast; hearing of Tingchen's leniency, many laid down arms and came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal holdouts heard of his leniency and many laid down arms and submitted.

sentences.zh: 六年，以病乞休，詔慰留之。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, on account of illness he requested retirement; an edict comforted him and kept him in post.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 6 he asked to retire for illness; the throne refused and urged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 八年，巡海自福建還，至奉化，病卒，諡清獻。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, while patrolling the sea he returned from Fujian; at Fenghua he died of illness; posthumous title Qingxian.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 8, returning from a coastal inspection in Fujian, he fell ill and died at Fenghua; posthumous title Qingxian.

sentences.zh: 廷臣為政寬靜而善折獄。

translations.literal: Tingchen governed with leniency and calm yet was skilled at deciding cases.
translations.idiomatic: Tingchen ruled with calm leniency yet was a sharp judge.

sentences.zh: 有瞽者入屠者室，攫其{}中錢，屠者逐之，則曰：「欺吾瞽，奪吾錢。」

translations.literal: A blind man entered a butcher's room and grabbed money from inside his cash box; the butcher chased him, and he said: "You bully a blind man and steal my money."
translations.idiomatic: A blind man entered a butcher's shop and snatched money from the cash box; when the butcher chased him, he cried, "You bully a blind man and steal my money."

sentences.zh: 廷臣令投錢水中，見浮脂，以錢還屠者。

translations.literal: Tingchen ordered the coins thrown into water; seeing floating grease, he returned the money to the butcher.
translations.idiomatic: Tingchen had the coins thrown into water; grease floated up, and he returned the money to the butcher.

sentences.zh: 有殺人獄已誣服，廷臣察傷格，曰：「傷寸而刃尺，必冤也！」

translations.literal: In a homicide case the accused had already falsely confessed; Tingchen examined the wound pattern and said: "A wound an inch wide but a blade a foot long—this must be a wrongful case!"
translations.idiomatic: In a murder case the accused had already confessed; Tingchen examined the wounds and said, "An inch-wide wound from a foot-long blade—that cannot be right!"

sentences.zh: 更求之，得真殺人者。

translations.literal: He searched again and obtained the real killer.
translations.idiomatic: A new search found the real killer.

sentences.zh: 旱，山中人言魃見，入人家輒失財物。

translations.literal: During drought, people in the mountains said a drought demon was seen and that upon entering households property was always lost.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought, mountain folk said a drought demon was stealing from homes.

sentences.zh: 廷臣曰：「盜也！」

translations.literal: Tingchen said: "A thief!"
translations.idiomatic: Tingchen said, "Thieves!"

sentences.zh: 令吏捕治之。

translations.literal: He ordered clerks to arrest and punish them.
translations.idiomatic: He had officers arrest them.

sentences.zh: 袁懋功，字九敘，順天香河人。

translations.literal: Yuan Maogong, courtesy name Jiuxu, was a native of Xianghe in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Maogong, courtesy name Jiuxu, was from Xianghe in Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 順治二年進士，授禮科給事中。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the second year of Shunzhi, he was appointed supervising secretary of the Ministry of Rites section.
translations.idiomatic: A Shunzhi 2 jinshi, he became a supervising secretary in the Ministry of Rites section.

sentences.zh: 疏請慎簡學官，磨勘文體，釐定禮制。

translations.literal: He memorialized requesting careful selection of school officials, scrutiny of literary style, and clarification of ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for careful selection of school officials, review of examination style, and clarification of ritual rules.

sentences.zh: 又以前明廢官援恩詔踵至，請敕吏部會都察院嚴覈才品。

translations.literal: Also, because dismissed Ming officials kept arriving citing amnesty edicts in succession, he requested an edict to the Board of Personnel jointly with the Censorate to scrutinize talent and character strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Dismissed Ming officials kept arriving citing amnesty edicts; he asked the Board of Personnel and Censorate to scrutinize them strictly.

sentences.zh: 累擢戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of the Board of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of the Board of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 十七年，世祖諭懋功才品敏練，授雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the Shizu Emperor remarked that Maogong's talent and character were keen and practiced, and appointed him provincial governor of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 17 the Shizu Emperor said Maogong was capable and made him provincial governor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 時雲南初定，懋功令降卒入籍歸農，墾無主之田。

translations.literal: At that time Yunnan had just been pacified; Maogong ordered surrendered soldiers to register and return to farming and to open ownerless fields.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan had just been pacified; Maogong registered surrendered troops as farmers and opened ownerless land.

sentences.zh: 編保甲，以時稽察。

translations.literal: He organized baojia and inspected them on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: He organized baojia units and inspected them regularly.

sentences.zh: 奏減屯田糧額，請停派部員履勘田畝。

translations.literal: He memorialized to reduce the grain quota on military colonies and requested cessation of dispatching ministry personnel to survey fields on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He cut military-colony grain quotas and stopped ministry survey teams from measuring fields in person.

sentences.zh: 撫雲南九載，政績大著。

translations.literal: As governor of Yunnan for nine years, his administrative achievements were greatly notable.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Yunnan nine years with outstanding results.

sentences.zh: 以父憂去。

translations.literal: He left office on account of his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his father.

sentences.zh: 服除，起山東巡撫。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was recalled as provincial governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was made provincial governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 康熙十年，濟南五十六州縣衛新墾地被淹，懋功疏請展限一年起科，部格不行，上特允之。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Kangxi, newly opened fields in the fifty-six prefectures, counties, and garrisons of Jinan were inundated; Maogong memorialized requesting extension of the deadline one year before levying tax; the ministry rejected it, but the emperor specially granted it.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 10 newly opened fields in fifty-six Jinan jurisdictions were flooded; Maogong asked a one-year delay before taxing them; the ministry refused, but the emperor granted it.

sentences.zh: 調浙江，未行，卒，諡清獻。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Zhejiang but before departing died; posthumous title Qingxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Zhejiang but died before taking up the post; posthumous title Qingxian.

sentences.zh: 徐旭齡，字元文，浙江錢塘人。

translations.literal: Xu Xuling, courtesy name Yuanwen, was a native of Qiantang in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Xuling, courtesy name Yuanwen, was from Qiantang in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年進士，除刑部主事，再遷禮部郎中。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the twelfth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed a principal clerk of the Board of Punishments and was twice transferred to director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: A Shunzhi 12 jinshi, he became a principal clerk in the Board of Punishments and later director in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，授雲南道御史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi he was appointed censor of the Yunnan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 6 he became censor of the Yunnan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 裁缺，改湖廣道。

translations.literal: When his post was abolished he was changed to the Huguang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When his post was cut he moved to the Huguang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 迭疏請汰額外衙役，核州縣贖鍰，降調官百姓保留敕督撫核實，皆下部議行。

translations.literal: In succession he memorialized requesting elimination of supernumerary yamen runners, verification of redemption fines in prefectures and counties, and retention of commoners for demoted officials pending edicts to governors to verify—all were referred to the ministries for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly asked to cut supernumerary runners, audit redemption fines, and require governors to verify commoners retained for demoted officials—all were sent to the ministries.

sentences.zh: 命偕御史席特納巡視兩淮鹽政，疏陳積弊，請嚴禁斤重不得逾額，部議如所請勒石。

translations.literal: He was ordered together with Censor Xite'na to inspect the Lianghuai salt administration; he memorialized stating accumulated abuses and requested strict prohibition of weight exceeding quota; the ministry deliberated as requested and had it carved in stone.
translations.idiomatic: With Censor Xite'na he inspected Lianghuai salt, exposed long-standing abuses, and asked strict weight limits; the ministry agreed and had the rule carved in stone.

sentences.zh: 又疏請停止豫徵鹽課，部議不允。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting cessation of advance collection of salt tax; the ministry deliberated and did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to end advance salt-tax collection; the ministry refused.

sentences.zh: 遷太常寺少卿，累擢左僉都御史，請裁軍興以後增設道員。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was repeatedly promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, and requested abolition of circuit intendant posts added after military campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, rose to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, and asked to abolish circuit posts added after the wars.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，授山東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed provincial governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 22 he was made provincial governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，遷工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was transferred to vice minister of the Board of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 23 he became vice minister of the Board of Works.

sentences.zh: 復出為漕運總督，疏請釐三害，籌三便，革隨漕增、裁運耗二項，及民間幫貼盤費腳價，各省給軍款項，改由州縣迳發運丁，行月糧改入現運項下撥給，並合併漕船幫次，皆下九卿議行。

translations.literal: He went out again as Grand Canal transport governor-general, memorializing to rectify three harms and plan three conveniences, abolishing the two items of increases along with grain transport and cuts to transport wastage, as well as popular supplementary payments for porterage and cartage, having each province's military funds issued directly by prefectures and counties to transport laborers, putting monthly grain rations into current transport accounts for allocation, and merging transport boat squadrons—all were sent to the Nine Ministers for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: He then became Grand Canal transport governor-general, proposing reforms to end three abuses and secure three benefits: ending transport surcharges and wastage cuts, private porterage fees, and provincial military payments to boatmen; having counties pay transport workers directly; folding monthly rations into current transport accounts; and merging boat squadrons—all went to the Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，卒，亦諡清獻。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he died; he too received posthumous title Qingxian.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 26 he died; he too received the posthumous title Qingxian.

sentences.zh: 郎廷佐，字一柱，漢軍鑲黃旗人，世籍廣寧。

translations.literal: Lang Tingzuo, courtesy name Yizhu, was a member of the Hanjun Bordered Yellow Banner with hereditary registration at Guangning.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Tingzuo, courtesy name Yizhu, was of the Hanjun Bordered Yellow Banner, with hereditary registration at Guangning.

sentences.zh: 父熙載，明諸生。

translations.literal: His father Xizai was a licentiate of Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xizai was a Ming licentiate.

sentences.zh: 太祖克廣寧，熙載來歸，授防禦，以軍功予世職游擊。

translations.literal: When Taizu took Guangning, Xizai came to submit, was granted defense commandant, and for military merit was given the hereditary rank of guerrilla.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took Guangning, Xizai submitted, became defense commandant, and earned the hereditary rank of guerrilla.

sentences.zh: 崇德元年卒，長子廷輔嗣。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Chongde; the eldest son Tingfu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Chongde 1; eldest son Tingfu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 廷佐，其次子也。

translations.literal: Tingzuo was the second son.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzuo was the second son.

sentences.zh: 自官學生授內院筆帖式，擢國史院侍讀。

translations.literal: From palace student he was appointed a clerk in the inner court, and was promoted to reader in the National History Academy.
translations.idiomatic: From palace student he became an inner-court clerk, then reader in the National History Academy.

sentences.zh: 順治三年，從肅親王豪格徇四川，平張獻忠。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shunzhi he followed Prince Su Hoge through Sichuan and pacified Zhang Xianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 3 he followed Prince Su Hoge into Sichuan and helped pacify Zhang Xianzhong.

sentences.zh: 六年，從英親王阿濟格討叛將薑瓖。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he followed Prince Ying Ajige in campaigning against the rebel Jiang Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 6 he followed Prince Ying Ajige against the rebel Jiang Xiang.

sentences.zh: 遷秘書院學士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to academician of the Secretariat Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He became an academician of the Secretariat Academy.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授江西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed provincial governor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 11 he was made provincial governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 江西自明末洊遭兵亂，逋賦鉅萬。

translations.literal: Jiangxi since late Ming had repeatedly suffered military disorder, with tax arrears in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi since late Ming had seen repeated warfare and tax arrears in the millions.

sentences.zh: 廷佐累疏請蠲緩蘇民困，詔允行。

translations.literal: Tingzuo repeatedly memorialized requesting remission and relief to ease the people's hardship; edicts approved implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzuo repeatedly asked for remissions and relief; the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 土寇洪國柱等掠饒州、廣信，遣​​兵剿平之。

translations.literal: The native bandits Hong Guozhu and others plundered Raozhou and Guangxin; he dispatched troops and suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: Native bandits Hong Guozhu and others raided Raozhou and Guangxin; he sent troops and suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 十二年，擢江南江西總督。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted to governor-general of Jiangnan and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 12 he was made governor-general of Jiangnan and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 江南逋賦至四百餘萬，廷佐覈賦籍，曰：「此非盡民困不能輸也，必有官吏侵蝕而詭稱民逋者。

translations.literal: Jiangnan's tax arrears reached more than four million; Tingzuo examined the tax registers and said: "This is not entirely because the people are in hardship and cannot pay; there must be officials who embezzle and falsely claim popular arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan's arrears topped four million taels; Tingzuo audited the registers and said, "This is not all popular hardship—officials must be embezzling and calling it popular arrears.

sentences.zh: 民困可矜，官吏弊不可不革。」

translations.literal: Popular hardship deserves pity; official abuses cannot go unreformed."
translations.idiomatic: Popular hardship deserves pity; official abuse must be reformed."

sentences.zh: 乃籍之為三：曰官侵，曰吏蝕，曰民逋。

translations.literal: He then registered them in three categories: called official embezzlement, called clerk erosion, called popular arrears.
translations.idiomatic: He split the books into three categories: official embezzlement, clerk theft, and genuine popular arrears.

sentences.zh: 責右布政使按籍督催，而令左布政使稽徵新賦，以除新舊牽混之弊。

translations.literal: He charged the right provincial administration commissioner to press collection according to the registers, while ordering the left commissioner to audit collection of new taxes, to remove the abuse of old and new being tangled together.
translations.idiomatic: The right commissioner pressed old arrears by category; the left audited new taxes—ending the mix of old and new.

sentences.zh: 並疏請官吏徵賦未完者，令戴罪留任催徵，於是宿弊頓革。

translations.literal: He also memorialized requesting that officials who had not finished tax collection be ordered to remain in post bearing guilt and press collection; thereby long-standing abuses were suddenly reformed.
translations.idiomatic: He also let officials who had not finished collection stay in post under discipline to finish the job; long-standing abuses collapsed at once.

sentences.zh: 師行取估舶以濟，商民交困。

translations.literal: When armies marched they took merchant vessels by assessment to supply needs, and merchants and commoners were alike distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Armies requisitioned merchant ships for transport and merchants suffered.

sentences.zh: 廷佐疏請視江西例，發帑造船備用，上韙其言，命議行。

translations.literal: Tingzuo memorialized requesting that following the Jiangxi precedent, treasury funds be issued to build ships for reserve; the emperor approved his words and ordered deliberation for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzuo asked, as in Jiangxi, to build reserve ships with treasury funds; the emperor approved and ordered implementation.

sentences.zh: 十六年，巡閱江海，因密疏言：「鄭成功屯聚海島，將犯江南。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, while inspecting rivers and sea, he submitted a secret memorial saying: "Zheng Chenggong is massed on sea islands and is about to invade Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 16, inspecting the coast, he sent a secret memorial: "Zheng Chenggong is massed on the islands and will strike Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 江南汛兵無多，水師舟楫未備，請調發鄰省勁兵防禦。」

translations.literal: Jiangnan's garrison troops are not numerous, naval ships and boats are not prepared; I request mobilizing crack troops from neighboring provinces for defense."
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan has few garrison troops and no ready fleet; send crack troops from neighboring provinces."

sentences.zh: 事格不行。

translations.literal: The matter was blocked and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: The request was blocked.

sentences.zh: 未幾，成功陷鎮江，襲瓜洲，遂窺江寧，城守單弱。

translations.literal: Before long Chenggong took Zhenjiang, raided Guazhou, and then watched for an opening against Jiangning; the city's defense was thin and weak.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chenggong took Zhenjiang, raided Guazhou, and menaced Jiangning; the city's defenses were thin.

sentences.zh: 會梅勒額真噶楚哈、瑪爾賽自貴州旋師，廷佐與駐防總管喀喀木邀入城共禦敵，挫其前鋒，得舟二十餘。

translations.literal: It happened that Meirei Ejen Gachuha and Ma'ersai were returning their armies from Guizhou; Tingzuo together with Garrison Commander Kakemu invited them into the city to jointly resist the enemy, checked their vanguard, and captured more than twenty boats.
translations.idiomatic: Meirei Ejen Gachuha and Ma'ersai were returning from Guizhou; Tingzuo and Garrison Commander Kakemu brought them into the city, checked the vanguard, and captured twenty-odd boats.

sentences.zh: 成功兵大至，戰艦蔽江，廷佐登埤固守。

translations.literal: Chenggong's troops arrived in force; warships covered the river; Tingzuo mounted the ramparts and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong's main force arrived and warships filled the river; Tingzuo held the walls.

sentences.zh: 提督管效忠、總兵梁化鳳等水陸夾擊，焚敵艦五百餘，擒斬無算，成功遁入海。

translations.literal: Provincial Military Commissioner Guan Xiaozhong, Regional Commander Liang Huafeng, and others struck from land and water; they burned more than five hundred enemy vessels, captured and beheaded beyond counting, and Chenggong fled into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Military Commissioner Guan Xiaozhong and Regional Commander Liang Huafeng struck from land and sea, burned five hundred enemy ships, killed countless men, and Chenggong fled to sea.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, an edict praised and rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Victory was reported and the throne praised and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 十八年，分江南江西總督為二，以廷佐專督江南。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year the Jiangnan-Jiangxi governor-generalship was divided in two; Tingzuo supervised Jiangnan alone.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 18 the post was split; Tingzuo governed Jiangnan alone.

sentences.zh: 康熙四年，復舊制，仍兼江西。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kangxi the old system was restored and he again held Jiangxi concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 4 the old combined post was restored.

sentences.zh: 七年，以疾解任。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he left office on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 7 he left office for illness.

sentences.zh: 致仕大學士金之俊家居，得匿名書帖，詆其曾降李自成，之俊訴廷佐，令有司窮治。

translations.literal: Retired Grand Secretary Jin Zhijun was at home and received an anonymous letter slandering him for having once surrendered to Li Zicheng; Zhijun complained to Tingzuo, who ordered the local officials to investigate thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Retired Grand Secretary Jin Zhijun received an anonymous letter accusing him of once surrendering to Li Zicheng; he complained to Tingzuo, who ordered a full investigation.

sentences.zh: 上聞，慮株連無辜，責之俊違例妄訴，廷佐俟病痊起用，鐫二秩。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, fearing implicating the innocent, he reproached Zhijun for violating regulations in a reckless complaint; Tingzuo was to await recovery from illness before reuse, and was demoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feared innocent people would be swept up, rebuked Zhijun for a improper complaint, ordered Tingzuo held for reuse after recovery, and cut him two ranks.

sentences.zh: 十三年，耿精忠反，授廷佐福建總督。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Geng Jingzhong rebelled; Tingzuo was appointed governor-general of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13 Geng Jingzhong rebelled; Tingzuo was made governor-general of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 廷佐奏​​言：「臣孫為耿氏婿，臣與精忠有連。

translations.literal: Tingzuo memorialized saying: "Your subject's grandson is son-in-law to the Geng clan; your subject is connected with Jingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzuo wrote: "My grandson married into the Geng clan; I am kin to Jingzhong.

sentences.zh: 然誓不與賊俱生，原力疾前驅，殲除叛寇。」

translations.literal: Yet I swear not to live together with the rebels; I wish, exerting my strength despite illness, to advance at the fore and exterminate the rebel bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I swear not to live while they do; though ill, I ask to lead the van and destroy the rebels."

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，賜鞍馬、甲胄以寵其行。

translations.literal: The emperor praised this and bestowed saddle horses and armor to honor his departure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him and granted saddle horses and armor to send him off in honor.

sentences.zh: 廷佐至浙江，從大將軍康親王杰書治軍，駐金華。

translations.literal: Tingzuo reached Zhejiang, followed the great general Prince Kang Jieshu in managing the army, and was stationed at Jinhua.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzuo reached Zhejiang, joined the great general Prince Kang Jieshu in command, and encamped at Jinhua.

sentences.zh: 疏陳精忠句結海寇，宜剿撫兼施。

translations.literal: He memorialized stating that Jingzhong was in league with sea pirates and that suppression and pacification should be applied together.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote that Jingzhong was allied with sea pirates and that force and leniency should be used together.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「海寇當撫，精忠當用剿，或用間。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Sea pirates should be pacified; Jingzhong should be handled with suppression, or by stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Pacify the sea pirates; strike Jingzhong—or use stratagem."

sentences.zh: 廷佐頗有規畫，未及行，十五年，卒於軍，賜祭葬。

translations.literal: Tingzuo had considerable plans but before carrying them out, in the fifteenth year he died in camp; funeral sacrifices were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzuo had sound plans but died in camp in Kangxi 15 before carrying them out; the court granted funeral honors.

sentences.zh: 江南、江西俱祀名宦。

translations.literal: Both Jiangnan and Jiangxi enshrined him among eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was enshrined among eminent officials in both Jiangnan and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 弟廷相，字鈞衡。

translations.literal: His younger brother Tingxiang, courtesy name Junheng.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Tingxiang, courtesy name Junheng.

sentences.zh: 初授欽天監筆帖式。

translations.literal: He was first appointed a clerk in the Directorate of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as a clerk in the Directorate of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 累官四川左布政使。

translations.literal: Through successive posts he reached left provincial administration commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to left provincial commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 四川屢經兵燹，廷相蒞任，百廢俱興，民不知擾。

translations.literal: Sichuan had repeatedly suffered military devastation; when Tingxiang took office, a hundred neglected tasks were revived together, and the people did not feel harassment.
translations.idiomatic: Sichuan had been ravaged by war; when Tingxiang arrived, abandoned projects were revived and the people scarcely noticed the transition.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，授河南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Kangxi he was appointed provincial governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 8 he was made provincial governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 廷佐卒，上即擢廷相為福建總督。

translations.literal: When Tingzuo died, the emperor immediately promoted Tingxiang to governor-general of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingzuo died, the throne at once made Tingxiang governor-general of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 會精忠降，餘黨紀朝佐、張八等尚抗拒，廷相剿撫兼用，旬月悉平。

translations.literal: When Jingzhong surrendered, remnant partisans Ji Chaozuo, Zhang Ba, and others still resisted; Tingxiang used suppression and pacification together, and within a month all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: After Jingzhong surrendered, holdouts Ji Chaozuo, Zhang Ba, and others still fought on; Tingxiang combined force and leniency and within a month had pacified them all.

sentences.zh: 鄭錦及山寇硃寅屢犯郡縣，遣兵分剿，屢卻之，擒斬甚眾。

translations.literal: Zheng Jing and the mountain bandit Zhu Yin repeatedly invaded prefectures and counties; he dispatched troops in separate columns to suppress them, repeatedly drove them back, and captured and beheaded very many.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jing and the mountain bandit Zhu Yin raided county after county; he sent columns against them, beat them back repeatedly, and killed or captured a great number.

sentences.zh: 十七年，錦窺漳州，據玉州等寨，分擾石碼、江東橋。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Jing watched for an opening at Zhangzhou, seized camps such as Yuzhou, and sent detachments to harass Shima and Jiangdong Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 17 Jing menaced Zhangzhou, seized camps including Yuzhou, and raided Shima and Jiangdong Bridge.

sentences.zh: 廷相請援，詔康親王督兵協剿。

translations.literal: Tingxiang requested reinforcements; an edict ordered Prince Kang to supervise troops in joint suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Tingxiang asked for help; the throne ordered Prince Kang to lead joint operations.

sentences.zh: 時寇勢甚張，上責廷相庸懦不能殄賊，命解任。

translations.literal: At that time the bandits' power was very great; the emperor reproached Tingxiang as timid and weak and unable to exterminate the rebels, and ordered his dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were at their peak; the emperor blamed Tingxiang for timidity and failure to destroy them and removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 27.

sentences.zh: 郎永清，字定庵。

translations.literal: Lang Yongqing, courtesy name Ding'an.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Yongqing, courtesy name Ding'an.

sentences.zh: 初授禮部筆帖式。

translations.literal: He was first appointed a clerk in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as a Ministry of Rites clerk.

sentences.zh: 出知山西渾源州，招民開墾，豁逋賦萬餘。

translations.literal: He went out as magistrate of Hunyuan Prefecture in Shanxi, induced the people to open wasteland for cultivation, and remitted more than ten thousand in tax arrears.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Hunyuan in Shanxi, he brought settlers to open land and remitted more than ten thousand taels in arrears.

sentences.zh: 姜瓖黨高山等竄伏山谷間為盜，永清簡丁壯，親率搜捕，多斬獲。

translations.literal: Followers of Jiang Xiang such as Gaoshan hid in mountain valleys as bandits; Yongqing selected strong young men, personally led search and capture, and captured or beheaded many.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xiang's followers Gaoshan and others hid in the hills as bandits; Yongqing picked militia, led the hunt himself, and took many.

sentences.zh: 事平，擢江西贛州知府，平反冤獄，居官有聲。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he was promoted to prefect of Ganzhou in Jiangxi, reversed wrongful convictions, and had a reputation in office.
translations.idiomatic: When order returned he became prefect of Ganzhou in Jiangxi, cleared wrongful cases, and won a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 師討李定國，議牧馬贛州，民譁言兵且入城，爭竄避。

translations.literal: When the army campaigned against Li Dingguo, it was proposed to pasture horses at Ganzhou; the people clamored that troops were about to enter the city and scrambled to flee.
translations.idiomatic: The army marching against Li Dingguo proposed to pasture horses at Ganzhou; rumor spread that troops would enter the city and people fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 永清度城外地為牧場，區畫八旗駐營，具芻茭，兵不入城，贛民安堵。

translations.literal: Yongqing designated land outside the walls as pasture, laid out Eight Banner encampments, provided fodder, kept troops from entering the city, and the people of Ganzhou lived undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Yongqing set aside pasture outside the walls, arranged Eight Banner camps and fodder, kept soldiers out of the city, and Ganzhou stayed calm.

sentences.zh: 師還，徵民夫數千挽舟，灘水湍激，永清慮民夫無食且逃，以大艦載米尾其後，軍行無滯。

translations.literal: When the army returned, several thousand corvée laborers were levied to tow boats; the shoal waters ran swift and fierce; Yongqing feared the laborers would have no food and flee, and had a large ship carry rice trailing behind them, so the army's march had no delay.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march thousands of laborers towed boats through rapids; fearing hunger and desertion, Yongqing sent a grain ship to follow them and the army never stalled.

sentences.zh: 民德之，為立像祠焉。

translations.literal: The people were grateful to him and erected a statue shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: Grateful citizens raised a statue in his honor.

sentences.zh: 從子廷佐巡撫江西，永清例迴避，調山西汾州。

translations.literal: His nephew Tingzuo was provincial governor of Jiangxi; Yongqing by regulation recused himself and was transferred to Fenzhou in Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Tingzuo governed Jiangxi; Yongqing recused himself by rule and was moved to Fenzhou in Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 遷山東東昌道副使，轉湖廣下荊南道。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice commissioner of the Dongchang circuit in Shandong, then to the Xianan lower circuit in Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice commissioner of Shandong's Dongchang circuit, then of Huguang's lower Xianan circuit.

sentences.zh: 李自成黨踞房、竹間，官軍分路會剿，餽餉俱取給鄖、襄，陸路挽運，議徵民夫數万。

translations.literal: Li Zicheng's partisans held the Fang and Zhu region; government troops converged by separate routes to suppress them; supplies all had to be drawn from Yun and Xiang by land transport, and levying tens of thousands of corvée laborers was proposed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zicheng's followers held the Fang-Zhu hills; converging government columns drew supplies from Yun and Xiang by land haul, and officials proposed levying tens of thousands of laborers.

sentences.zh: 永清疏水道，仿古轉搬法，安塘遞運，軍得無匱。

translations.literal: Yongqing opened waterways, following the ancient relay-transport method in establishing depot relays, and the army was never left wanting.
translations.idiomatic: Yongqing opened waterways and revived the old relay-transport system with depot chains, so the army never ran short.

sentences.zh: 累遷湖南布政使。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached provincial administration commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to provincial commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 衡、永、寶三郡苦食粵鹽，灘險道遠，商民交病。

translations.literal: The three prefectures Heng, Yong, and Bao suffered from consuming Guangdong salt—the shoals were dangerous and the route long, and merchants and commoners were alike afflicted.
translations.idiomatic: Heng, Yong, and Bao prefectures relied on Guangdong salt; treacherous shoals and long hauls hurt merchants and people alike.

sentences.zh: 永清申請改食淮鹽，民便之。

translations.literal: Yongqing requested permission to change to Huai salt; the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Yongqing won approval to switch to Huai salt, to the people's relief.

sentences.zh: 康熙十二年，調河南。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Kangxi he was transferred to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 12 he was transferred to Henan.

sentences.zh: 師討吳三桂，議養馬南陽，永清請移牧湖廣。

translations.literal: When the army campaigned against Wu Sangui, pasture at Nanyang was proposed; Yongqing requested moving the herds to Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Wu Sangui, the court proposed pasturing horses at Nanyang; Yongqing asked to shift the herds to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 河南協濟湖廣軍米十萬石，申巡撫題請改於江南、江西採運。

translations.literal: Henan was to supply one hundred thousand shi of army grain to Huguang; he reported to the governor and requested that procurement and transport be shifted to Jiangnan and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Henan owed Huguang a hundred thousand shi of army grain; he asked the governor to source it from Jiangnan and Jiangxi instead.

sentences.zh: 在官十二年，課最。

translations.literal: Twelve years in office, his assessment ranked highest.
translations.idiomatic: After twelve years in office his performance ranked first.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，擢山東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted to provincial governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 25 he was made provincial governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒官，祀湖南名宦。

translations.literal: Before long he died in office; he was enshrined among eminent officials of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he died in office and was enshrined among Hunan's eminent officials.

sentences.zh: 永清子廷極、廷棟。

translations.literal: Yongqing's sons were Tingji and Tingdong.
translations.idiomatic: Yongqing's sons were Tingji and Tingdong.

sentences.zh: 廷極，字紫衡。

translations.literal: Tingji, courtesy name Ziheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tingji, courtesy name Ziheng.

sentences.zh: 初授江寧府同知，遷雲南順寧知府，有政聲。

translations.literal: He was first appointed vice prefect of Jiangning Prefecture, was transferred to prefect of Shunning in Yunnan, and had a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He began as vice prefect of Jiangning, became prefect of Shunning in Yunnan, and earned a name for good government.

sentences.zh: 累擢江西巡撫。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached provincial governor of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to provincial governor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 江西多山，州縣運糧盤兌，民間津貼夫船耗米五斗三升，載賦役全書，歲分給如法。

translations.literal: Jiangxi is largely mountainous; when prefectures and counties transported grain for inspection and verification, the people's allowance for porters and boats was five dou three sheng of wastage grain, recorded in the complete book of tax and corvée labor, and distributed yearly according to rule.
translations.idiomatic: Mountainous Jiangxi required grain transport for inspections; porters and boats were paid five dou three sheng wastage per rules in the corvée register, disbursed yearly as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 戶部初議駁減，總督范承勳以請，得如故。

translations.literal: The Board of Revenue at first proposed rejecting the reduction; Governor-General Fan Chengxun petitioned on their behalf, and they received it as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Board of Revenue first tried to cut the allowance; Governor-General Fan Chengxun intervened and it stayed as before.

sentences.zh: 至是戶部复議停給，並追前已給者，廷極累疏爭之。

translations.literal: At this point the Board of Revenue again proposed halting payment and even recovering what had already been given; Tingji repeatedly memorialized disputing this.
translations.idiomatic: The Board then moved to stop payment and claw back past disbursements; Tingji memorialized repeatedly in protest.

sentences.zh: 尋兼理兩江總督。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently charged with administering the governor-generalship of Liangjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took on the Liangjiang governor-generalship as well.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，擢漕運總督。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year he was promoted to governor-general of grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 51 he was made governor-general of grain transport.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡溫勤。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous title Wennin.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumous title Wennin.

sentences.zh: 廷棟，字樸齋。

translations.literal: Tingdong, courtesy name Puzhai.
translations.idiomatic: Tingdong, courtesy name Puzhai.

sentences.zh: 官湖南按察使。

translations.literal: He served as provincial surveillance commissioner of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as provincial surveillance commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 佟鳳彩，字高岡，漢軍正藍旗人，養性從孫也。

translations.literal: Tong Fengcai, courtesy name Gaogang, was a member of the Hanjun Plain Blue Banner and a grand-nephew of Yangxing.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Fengcai, courtesy name Gaogang, was of the Hanjun Plain Blue Banner and a grand-nephew of Yangxing.

sentences.zh: 初授國史院副理事官。

translations.literal: He was first appointed associate director of the National History Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as associate director of the National History Academy.

sentences.zh: 外改順天香河知縣，內擢山西道御史，出視河東鹽政。
