translations.literal: Externally he was reassigned as magistrate of Xianghe in Shuntian; internally he was promoted censor of the Shanxi circuit and went out to oversee Hedong salt administration.
translations.idiomatic: He became magistrate of Xianghe in Shuntian, then censor of the Shanxi circuit overseeing Hedong salt.

sentences.zh: 順治七年，巡按湖南。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Shunzhi he toured and inspected Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 7 he conducted an inspection tour of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 八年，外轉湖廣武昌道參議，遷廣西右布政使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was externally transferred to participation commissioner of the Wuchang circuit in Huguang, and was moved to right provincial administration commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 8 he became participation commissioner of Huguang's Wuchang circuit, then right provincial commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 時師徵雲南，道廣西，供億浩繁，鳳彩籌濟無匱。

translations.literal: At that time the army campaigned against Yunnan and passed through Guangxi; supplies were vast and numerous, yet Fengcai provided for them without shortage.
translations.idiomatic: Armies marching on Yunnan crossed Guangxi with immense supply needs; Fengcai met them without fail.

sentences.zh: 調江西左布政使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to left provincial administration commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to left provincial commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 十七年，擢四川巡撫。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to provincial governor of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 17 he was made provincial governor of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 四川經張獻忠亂，城邑殘破，勸官吏捐輸，修築成都府城，葺治學宮，濬都江大堰。

translations.literal: Sichuan had suffered Zhang Xianzhong's rebellion; cities and towns lay in ruins; he urged officials to contribute donations, rebuilt the Chengdu prefectural walls, repaired the school palace, and dredged the great Dujiang irrigation works.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Xianzhong's devastation he urged officials to donate, rebuilt Chengdu's walls, restored the academy, and dredged the great Dujiang irrigation works.

sentences.zh: 以祖母憂去官。

translations.literal: On mourning for his grandmother he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his grandmother.

sentences.zh: 康熙六年，起貴州巡撫。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kangxi he was recalled as provincial governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 6 he was recalled as provincial governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「驛站累民，而貴州尤苦。

translations.literal: He memorialized saying: "Relay stations burden the people, and Guizhou suffers especially.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "Relay stations burden the people, and Guizhou suffers worst.

sentences.zh: 層山峻嶺，俗言'地無三里平'。

translations.literal: Layer upon layer of steep mountains—as the saying has it, 'nowhere three li of level ground.'
translations.idiomatic: Steep mountains rise in tiers; folk say, 'nowhere three li of level ground.'

sentences.zh: 行一站，馬則蹄瘤脊爛，夫則足破肩穿。

translations.literal: Cover one station and horses' hooves fester and backs break down; porters' feet split and shoulders wear through.
translations.idiomatic: One station's march leaves horses with hoof sores and broken backs and porters with split feet and torn shoulders.

sentences.zh: 應於重安江、楊老堡、黃絲鋪、盤江坡、江西坡、輭轎坡等六處增置腰站，設夫馬如額。」

translations.literal: At six places—Chong'an River, Yanglaobao, Huangsipu, Panjiang Slope, Jiangxi Slope, and Ruanchaiao Slope—waist relay stations should be added and porters and horses established to quota."
translations.idiomatic: Waist relay stations should be added at six points—Chong'an River, Yanglaobao, Huangsipu, Panjiang Slope, Jiangxi Slope, and Ruanchaiao Slope—with porters and horses set at full quota."

sentences.zh: 復言：「黔省田土多奇零，國初隸版圖，州縣衛所等官不諳賦役，任意牒報。

translations.literal: He further said: "Guizhou's farmland is mostly scattered plots; when the dynasty first brought it into the territory, prefectural, county, guard, and post officials did not understand tax and corvée, and reported as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "Guizhou land is mostly scattered plots; when the dynasty first annexed the province, local officials did not understand tax and corvée and reported figures at will.

sentences.zh: 戶部以明季賦役全書發黔訂正，原報多者不復更改，少者照數增添。

translations.literal: The Board of Revenue sent the Ming-era complete book of tax and corvée to Guizhou for correction: original reports that were too high were not changed further, while those too low were increased to the full amount.
translations.idiomatic: The Board sent the Ming corvée register to Guizhou for correction: inflated figures stood, but shortfalls were raised to the full assessment.

sentences.zh: 臣蒞任，酌定繇單規式，飭所司填給花戶，以杜私派。

translations.literal: When your subject took office, he set a standard form for corvée labor tickets, ordered the responsible offices to fill and issue them to registered households, to stop unauthorized levies.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office I set a standard corvée ticket and ordered offices to issue them to registered households, to stop unauthorized levies.

sentences.zh: 嗣各屬造報，此多彼縮，不能照則填給。

translations.literal: Subsequently each subordinate submitted reports with some too high and others too low, and they could not fill and issue according to rule.
translations.idiomatic: Later subordinates reported figures all over the map—some inflated, some shrunk—and tickets could no longer be issued by rule.

sentences.zh: 且田地名色甚多，錢糧輕重不一。

translations.literal: Moreover land categories and designations are very numerous, and tax assessments vary in weight.
translations.idiomatic: Land categories are many and tax rates uneven.

sentences.zh: 現飭所司清釐，更正賦役全書，以垂永久。」

translations.literal: Your subject is now ordering the responsible offices to clear and straighten accounts and correct the complete book of tax and corvée, that it may endure permanently."
translations.idiomatic: I am now ordering a full audit and correction of the corvée register for a lasting settlement."

sentences.zh: 詔並允行。

translations.literal: Edicts approved both and ordered implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were approved and ordered implemented.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He went into mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 十一年，起河南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was recalled as provincial governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 11 he was recalled as provincial governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 彰德舊有萬金渠，康熙七、八年水患三至，鳳彩奏請修濬，以弭民害。

translations.literal: Zhangde had the old Wanjin Canal; in the seventh and eighth years of Kangxi floods came three times; Fengcai memorialized requesting repair and dredging to stop the people's suffering.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangde's ancient Wanjin Canal flooded three times in Kangxi 7–8; Fengcai asked to repair and dredge it and end the harm.

sentences.zh: 尋疏言：「豫省歲修黃河，用夫多或至萬餘，俱按畝起派，僱直年需三四十萬，小民重困。

translations.literal: Soon he memorialized saying: "Henan yearly repairs the Yellow River, using more than ten thousand laborers at times, all levied by the mu; hired wages yearly require three to four hundred thousand, and the common people are heavily burdened.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he wrote: "Henan's annual Yellow River repairs sometimes require more than ten thousand laborers, all levied by the mu; yearly wages run to three or four hundred thousand taels, and the people are crushed.

sentences.zh: 請改為官僱，按通省地畝等則派銀，刊明繇單。

translations.literal: I request changing to official hiring, distributing silver according to the province-wide land mu grades, and publishing clear corvée labor tickets.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the state hire labor directly, assess silver by province-wide land grades, and publish clear corvée tickets.

sentences.zh: 若遇意外大工，再具題請旨。」

translations.literal: If unforeseen major works arise, another memorial may request instructions."
translations.idiomatic: If unforeseen major works arise, a separate memorial may seek instructions."

sentences.zh: 上以派銀僱夫仍屬累民，命並免之。

translations.literal: The emperor said distributing silver to hire laborers still amounted to burdening the people, and ordered exemption from all of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that silver assessments to hire labor still burdened the people and ordered the whole scheme waived.

sentences.zh: 十二年，鳳彩疏言：「均平里甲，直省通行。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year Fengcai memorialized saying: "Equalizing li and jia is implemented throughout the direct provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 12 Fengcai wrote: "Equalizing li and jia is standard in the metropolitan provinces.

sentences.zh: 河南雖有里甲之名，其實多者每里或五六百頃，少者止一二百頃，或寥寥數頃。

translations.literal: Henan though it has the names li and jia, in fact the larger ones have five or six hundred qing per li, the smaller only one or two hundred qing, or a bare few qing.
translations.idiomatic: Henan keeps the names li and jia, but some li hold five or six hundred qing while others hold only one or two hundred—or a bare few.

sentences.zh: 有司止知照例編差，裡小田少，難以承役，愈增苦累。

translations.literal: Local officials only know to assign corvée by precedent; where the li is small and land few, bearing corvée is hard, and hardship only increases.
translations.idiomatic: Officials assign corvée by rote; small li with little land cannot bear their share, and the burden grows worse.

sentences.zh: 今飭州縣按徵糧地畝冊，如一州縣有地一千頃，原分為十里者，每裡均分一百頃；

translations.literal: Your subject now orders prefectures and counties to follow the land-tax mu register: if one prefecture or county has one thousand qing of land originally divided into ten li, each li should share one hundred qing equally;
translations.idiomatic: I now order counties to follow the tax land register: if a county has one thousand qing divided into ten li, each li should hold one hundred qing;

sentences.zh: 一里之中各分十甲，每甲均分十頃。

translations.literal: within one li each is divided into ten jia, and each jia shares ten qing equally.
translations.idiomatic: each li is split into ten jia of ten qing apiece.

sentences.zh: 遇有差徭，按里甲分當，則豪強無計規避，貧弱不致偏枯。」

translations.literal: When corvée and labor service arise, assignment by li and jia shares the burden, so the powerful have no scheme to evade and the poor and weak do not suffer disproportionately."
translations.idiomatic: When corvée falls due, li and jia share it equally—the powerful cannot dodge and the poor are not crushed alone."

sentences.zh: 又言：「豫省民間栽柳供河工採辦，歲需百餘萬束。

translations.literal: He further said: "Henan commoners plant willows for river-works procurement; yearly need exceeds a million bundles.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Henan commoners plant willows for river works; yearly demand exceeds a million bundles.

sentences.zh: 自康熙七年以後，協濟江南河工已二百七十餘萬束。

translations.literal: Since the seventh year of Kangxi, aid supplied to Jiangnan river works has already exceeded two million seven hundred thousand bundles.
translations.idiomatic: Since Kangxi 7 Henan has supplied Jiangnan river works with more than 2.7 million bundles.

sentences.zh: 去歲陽武險工，無柳可用，將民間桃、李、梨、杏盡行斫伐，方事堵禦。

translations.literal: Last year at the Yangwu dangerous works, with no willows available, peach, plum, pear, and apricot trees among the people were all cut down before embankment work could proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Last year at Yangwu's critical breach, with no willows left, officials felled every peach, plum, pear, and apricot tree before they could build defenses.

sentences.zh: 是修防本省河工尚屬不敷，實難協濟外省。

translations.literal: Thus even repairing and defending this province's river works is still insufficient; truly it is hard to supply aid to other provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Henan cannot even supply its own river works; it truly cannot keep aiding other provinces.

sentences.zh: 且黃河渡船裝柳止二三百束，至無船之地，官吏束手，若非亟圖變通，必至誤運。

translations.literal: Moreover Yellow River ferry boats carry only two or three hundred bundles of willows; where there are no boats officials are helpless, and unless change is urgently planned, transport will surely be delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow River ferries carry only two or three hundred bundles; where there are no boats officials are helpless, and without reform deliveries will fail.

sentences.zh: 向例本省河工運柳，每束給銀五分，今遠運江南千里之外，止給銀四分五釐，民安得不賠累？

translations.literal: By precedent for this province's river works willow transport, each bundle is paid five fen of silver; now transporting far to Jiangnan beyond a thousand li, only four fen five li are paid—how can the people not suffer loss?
translations.idiomatic: Provincial river works pay five fen per bundle; hauling to Jiangnan a thousand li away pays only four fen five li—how can people not lose money?

sentences.zh: 乞敕河臣於江南僱船到豫，使民止備柳束輓運江乾。

translations.literal: I beg that the river commissioner be ordered to hire boats from Jiangnan to reach Henan, so the people need only prepare willow bundles and haul them to the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the river commissioner hire boats from Jiangnan to Henan so people need only cut bundles and haul them to the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 嗣後就江南鄰近無河患處，酌派協濟。

translations.literal: Thereafter aid should be assigned from places near Jiangnan free of river calamity, as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Jiangnan's safer nearby counties should share the burden as appropriate.

sentences.zh: 留河南有餘不盡之柳，以備本省河患，庶百姓稍得蘇息，大工不致遲誤。」

translations.literal: Leave Henan's surplus willows for this province's river calamities, that the common people may gain some relief and major works not be delayed."
translations.idiomatic: Keep Henan's surplus willows for local emergencies so people may breathe easier and major works stay on schedule."

sentences.zh: 疏入，並下九卿科道議行。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, both were sent to the Nine Ministers and censorate for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: Both memorials went to the Nine Ministers and censorate for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 河南民稱均里甲、蠲夫柳為利民二大疏。

translations.literal: The people of Henan called the equalizing of lijia and the exemption on labor and willows the two great relief memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Henan folk called the lijia reform and the labor-and-willow relief his two great memorials for the people.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂反，河南當通衢，鳳彩悉心調度，民不知擾。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui rebelled; Henan lay on the main thoroughfare; Fengcai devoted himself to coordination, and the people did not feel harassment.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled Henan lay on the main thoroughfare; Fengcai coordinated supplies tirelessly and the people scarcely felt the strain.

sentences.zh: 十三年，以疾乞休，許之，士民赴闕籥留。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, on account of illness he requested retirement; permission was granted, and gentry and commoners went to the palace gate to plead for his retention.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 13 he asked to retire for illness; the throne agreed, and gentry and commoners thronged the palace gate to beg him to stay.

sentences.zh: 左都御史姚文然疏言，鳳彩撫豫數載，民所愛戴，宜令力疾視事，命仍留任。

translations.literal: Left Censor-in-Chief Yao Wenran memorialized, saying that Fengcai had governed Henan for several years and was beloved by the people; he should be ordered to attend to duties despite illness, and was commanded to remain in office.
translations.idiomatic: Left Censor-in-Chief Yao Wenran memorialized that Tong Fengcai had governed Henan for several years to the people's love, and ought to be told to carry on despite illness; the throne ordered him to stay in post.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒官，諡勤僖。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died in office and was posthumously titled Qinxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 16 he died in office and was given the posthumous title Qinxi, Diligent and Joyful.

sentences.zh: 河南、四川、貴州並祀名宦。

translations.literal: He was enshrined among notable officials in Henan, Sichuan, and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shrines to him as a notable official were raised in Henan, Sichuan, and Guizhou alike.

sentences.zh: 麻勒吉，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Ma Leiji, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Leiji, of the Guwalgiya clan, belonged to the Plain Yellow Banner of the Manchu Eight Banners.

sentences.zh: 先世居蘇完，有達邦阿者，當太祖時來歸，麻勒吉其曾孫也。

translations.literal: His ancestors dwelt in Suwan; one Tabang'a submitted in the time of the Taizu, and Ma Leiji was his great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: The family had lived in Suwan; an ancestor named Tabang'a came over in the Taizu era, and Ma Leiji was his great-grandson.

sentences.zh: 順治九年，滿、漢分榜，麻勒吉以繙譯舉人舉會試第一，殿試一甲第一，授修撰，世祖器之。

translations.literal: In Shunzhi 9, with separate examination rolls for Manchu and Han, Ma Leiji, as a translation licentiate, placed first in the metropolitan examination and first in the palace examination among the top tier; he was appointed Hanlin Compiler, and the Shizu emperor valued him.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 9, when Manchu and Han candidates sat separate rolls, Ma Leiji—already a translation licentiate—topped both the metropolitan and palace examinations as head of the first class; made a Hanlin compiler, he won the Shizu emperor's high regard.

sentences.zh: 十年，諭麻勒吉兼通滿、漢文，氣度老成，擢弘文院侍講學士。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the throne instructed that Ma Leiji was fluent in both Manchu and Chinese and mature in bearing, and promoted him to Vice Director of Lecturers in the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 10 the court noted his mastery of Manchu and Chinese and his seasoned bearing, and raised him to vice director of lecturers in the Hongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 十一年，擢學士，充日講官，教習庶吉士，編纂太祖、太宗聖訓副總裁，經筵講官。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Academician, served as Daily Lecturer, instructed expected Hanlin scholars, was deputy chief compiler of the Sacred Instructions of the Taizu and Taizong, and was a lecturer at the classics colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 11 he became an academician, daily lecturer, and instructor of expected Hanlin scholars, served as deputy chief compiler of the Taizu and Taizong Sacred Instructions, and lectured at the imperial classics colloquium.

sentences.zh: 明將孫可望詣經略洪承疇軍降，封義王，命麻勒吉為使，學士胡兆龍、奇徹伯副之，齎敕印授之，即偕詣京師。

translations.literal: The Ming general Sun Kewang came to surrender to Commissioner-General Hong Chengchou's army and was ennobled Prince of Righteousness; Ma Leiji was appointed envoy, with Academician Hu Zhaolong and Qichebo as deputies, to carry the imperial patent and seal to invest him, and then together proceeded to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming general Sun Kewang surrendered to Commissioner-General Hong Chengchou and was ennobled Prince of Righteousness, Ma Leiji was sent as chief envoy with Academician Hu Zhaolong and Qichebo as deputies to deliver the patent and seal and escort him straight to the capital.

sentences.zh: 麻勒吉初與直隸總督張玄錫同官學士，使還，玄錫迎於順德，麻勒吉訶辱之，玄錫憤，自剄不殊。

translations.literal: Ma Leiji had earlier been fellow academicians with Zhili Governor-General Zhang Xuanxi; on returning from the mission, Xuanxi welcomed him at Shunde, and Ma Leiji berated and humiliated him; Xuanxi, in rage, cut his own throat but did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Leiji and Zhili Governor-General Zhang Xuanxi had once been fellow academicians; when Ma returned from his mission, Xuanxi met him at Shunde, only to be reviled and shamed—whereupon Xuanxi, in fury, slashed his own throat but survived.

sentences.zh: 巡撫董天機以玄錫手書遺疏上聞，上遣學士折庫納、侍郎霍達往按。

translations.literal: Governor Dong Tianji reported Xuanxi's handwritten final memorial to the throne, and the emperor sent Academician Zhekenna and Vice Minister Huoda to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Dong Tianji forwarded Xuanxi's handwritten death testament to the throne, and the emperor dispatched Academician Zhekenna and Vice Minister Huoda to look into the affair.

sentences.zh: 玄錫复疏言：「麻勒吉於迎候時面斥失儀，又責以前此南行不出迎，且云：'在南方洪經略日有饋遺，何等盡禮！

translations.literal: Xuanxi again memorialized, saying: "When Ma Leiji was received in welcome, he rebuked me to my face in breach of propriety, and also blamed me for not going out to welcome him on his earlier journey south, saying: 'When Field Marshal Hong was in the south there were gifts every day—what courtesy was not shown!
translations.idiomatic: Xuanxi memorialized again: "At the welcoming ceremony Ma Leiji publicly upbraided me out of all propriety, and also reproached me for not having gone out to greet him on his earlier southern mission, saying, 'When Field Marshal Hong was in the south, gifts arrived daily—what courtesy did he lack!

sentences.zh: '奇徹伯又索臣騾駝。

translations.literal: Qichebo also demanded my mules and camels.
translations.idiomatic: Qichebo also demanded my mules and camels.

sentences.zh: 臣因賄賂幹禁，不與。」

translations.literal: Your subject, because bribery violated prohibition, did not give them.'"
translations.idiomatic: I refused, for bribery is forbidden.'"

sentences.zh: 上責麻勒吉等逼迫大臣，任意妄行，下九卿會勘。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked Ma Leiji and the others for pressuring great ministers and acting arbitrarily, and referred the case to joint investigation by the Nine Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor censured Ma Leiji and his party for browbeating a senior minister and acting at will, and ordered the Nine Ministers to investigate jointly.

sentences.zh: 玄錫，直隸清苑人，明庶吉士。

translations.literal: Xuanxi, a native of Qingyuan in Zhili, had been an expected Hanlin scholar under the Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuanxi was from Qingyuan in Zhili and had served as an expected Hanlin scholar under the Ming.

sentences.zh: 順治初授原官，自檢討累遷至學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi he was restored to his former post and was promoted from proofreader through successive ranks to academician.
translations.idiomatic: In early Shunzhi he was restored to office and rose from proofreader through successive posts to academician.

sentences.zh: 上稱其勤敏，擢宣大總督，移督直隸、河南、山東。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his diligence and sharpness, promoted him to Xuanda Governor-General, and transferred him to govern Zhili, Henan, and Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: The throne praised his diligence and quickness of mind, made him Xuanda governor-general, and later transferred him to oversee Zhili, Henan, and Shandong.

sentences.zh: 至是，以聽勘詣京師，居僧寺，自縊。

translations.literal: At this point, summoned to the capital to await investigation, he lodged in a Buddhist temple and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Now summoned to the capital to face inquiry, he took lodging in a monastery and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 九卿議麻勒吉等當奪官籍沒，上寬之，削加級、奪誥敕而已。

translations.literal: The Nine Ministers deliberated that Ma Leiji and the others should be stripped of office and have their property confiscated; the emperor showed leniency and only reduced their rank grades and confiscated their patents of ennoblement.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Ministers recommended stripping Ma Leiji and his colleagues of office and property; the emperor was lenient and merely reduced their rank grades and seized their patents of ennoblement.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以雲南初定，發帑金三十萬，命麻勒吉偕尚書伊圖、左都御史能圖往賑，並按大將軍貝勒尚善縱兵擾民狀，麻勒吉為奏辨。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, because Yunnan had just been pacified, three hundred thousand taels were disbursed from the treasury, and Ma Leiji was ordered, together with Minister Yitu and Left Censor-in-Chief Nitu, to go for relief and also to investigate the case of Field Marshal Prince Shangshan allowing his troops to harass the people; Ma Leiji memorialized in his defense.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 16, with Yunnan newly settled, the court released three hundred thousand taels and sent Ma Leiji with Minister Yitu and Left Censor-in-Chief Nitu to relieve distress and investigate Field Marshal Prince Shangshan for letting his troops prey on the people; Ma Leiji filed a memorial in Shangshan's defense.

sentences.zh: 尋安親王岳樂覆勘，尚善兵入永昌掠民婦事實，麻勒吉坐徇庇，奪官。

translations.literal: Soon Prince An Yuele reinvestigated and established the fact that Shangshan's troops entered Yongchang and plundered commoners' wives; Ma Leiji was punished for shielding him and was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Prince An Yuele soon reinvestigated and confirmed that Shangshan's men had entered Yongchang and seized commoners' wives; Ma Leiji was found to have covered for him and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 十八年，命以原銜入直。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was ordered to enter inner service at his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 18 he was ordered back into inner service at his former rank.

sentences.zh: 上大漸，召麻勒吉與學士王熙撰擬遺詔，付內廷侍衛賈卜嘉進奏。

translations.literal: The emperor's illness worsened; he summoned Ma Leiji and Academician Wang Xi to draft the death testament and entrusted it to Inner Court guard Jia Bujia to present.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor's illness deepened, he called Ma Leiji and Academician Wang Xi to draft the death testament and handed the draft to Inner Court guard Jia Bujia to present.

sentences.zh: 上命麻勒吉懷詔草，俟上更衣畢，與賈卜嘉奏知皇太后，宣示諸王貝勒。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Ma Leiji to carry the draft in his bosom and, after the emperor had finished changing clothes, together with Jia Bujia report to the Empress Dowager and proclaim it to the princes and beile.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Ma Leiji to keep the draft on his person and, once the emperor had finished dressing, to join Jia Bujia in informing the Empress Dowager and proclaiming it to the princes and beile.

sentences.zh: 是夕上崩，麻勒吉遵旨將事。

translations.literal: That evening the emperor died, and Ma Leiji carried out the orders in managing the affair.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor died, and Ma Leiji carried out his orders to the letter.

sentences.zh: 旋授秘書院學士。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed Academician of the Secretariat Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made an academician of the Secretariat Academy.

sentences.zh: 康熙五年，擢刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 5 he was promoted to Vice Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 5 he was promoted to vice minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 七年，授江南江西總督。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Governor-General of Jiangnan and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 7 he was made governor-general of Jiangnan and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 時蘇州、松江頻遭水患，布政使慕天顏議濬吳淞江、劉河口，麻勒吉因與巡撫瑪祜疏請以各府漕折銀十四萬充工費。

translations.literal: At the time Suzhou and Songjiang frequently suffered from flooding; Provincial Administration Commissioner Mu Tianyan proposed dredging the Wusong River and the mouth of the Liuhe River, and Ma Leiji together with Governor Maku memorialized requesting that one hundred forty thousand taels of grain-transport conversion silver from the various prefectures be used for project costs.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou and Songjiang were then repeatedly flooded; Provincial Administration Commissioner Mu Tianyan proposed dredging the Wusong River and Liuhe estuary, and Ma Leiji joined Governor Maku in asking that 140,000 taels of grain-transport conversion silver from the prefectures fund the work.

sentences.zh: 淮、揚被水坍沒田地，請永免歲賦。

translations.literal: For fields in Huaiyang that had collapsed and been submerged by water, they requested permanent exemption from the annual tax.
translations.idiomatic: For Huaiyang fields washed away or submerged, they asked that the annual levy be waived in perpetuity.

sentences.zh: 詔並允行。

translations.literal: An edict approved both requests.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved both measures.

sentences.zh: 鎮江駐防兵訐將軍李顯貴、知府劉元輔侵冒錢糧，遣學士折爾肯等往按得實，麻勒吉坐不先舉發，並械系至京聽勘。

translations.literal: Garrison troops at Zhenjiang denounced General Li Xiangui and Prefect Liu Yuanfu for embezzling funds and grain; Academician Zhe'erken and others were sent to investigate and found the charges true; Ma Leiji was punished for not having reported the matter first, and both he and the accused were shackled and sent to the capital to await investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenjiang garrison troops accused General Li Xiangui and Prefect Liu Yuanfu of embezzling funds and grain; Academician Zhe'erken and others were sent to investigate and confirmed the charges; Ma Leiji was faulted for not having reported it first, and he and the accused were shackled and brought to the capital for inquiry.

sentences.zh: 給事中姚文然疏言麻勒吉罪狀未定，宜寬鎖系，上然之。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Yao Wenran memorialized that Ma Leiji's guilt had not yet been determined and that his shackling should be relaxed; the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Yao Wenran argued that Ma Leiji's guilt was still unsettled and that he should not be kept in irons; the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋命復任。

translations.literal: He was soon ordered to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered back to his post.

sentences.zh: 十二年，大計，左遷兵部督捕理事官。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, at the grand assessment, he was demoted to Vice Director of Military Affairs for bandit suppression.
translations.idiomatic: At the grand assessment of Kangxi 12 he was demoted to vice director of military affairs for bandit suppression.

sentences.zh: 吳三桂反，定南王孔有德壻孫延齡及提督馬雄以廣西叛應之。

translations.literal: Wu Sangui rebelled, and Prince of Dingnan Kong Youde's son-in-law Sun Yanling and Regional Commander Ma Xiong rebelled in Guangxi in response.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rose in rebellion, Prince of Dingnan Kong Youde's son-in-law Sun Yanling and Regional Commander Ma Xiong mutinied in Guangxi in his support.

sentences.zh: 十六年，命赴簡親王喇布軍，招撫延齡。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was ordered to go to Prince Jian Labu's army to entice Yanling to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 16 he was sent to Prince Jian Labu's army to win Sun Yanling over.

sentences.zh: 比至桂林，延齡已為三桂所殺，其部將劉彥明等率眾降。

translations.literal: By the time he reached Guilin, Yanling had already been killed by Wu Sangui, and his subordinate generals Liu Yanming and others led their troops to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Guilin, Wu Sangui had already killed Yanling, and subordinate generals such as Liu Yanming brought their men over.

sentences.zh: 十八年，詔麻勒吉赴廣西護諸軍，時雄已死，其子承廕降，授招義將軍，封伯爵。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year an edict ordered Ma Leiji to go to Guangxi to oversee the armies; at the time Ma Xiong was already dead, and his son Chengyin surrendered, was granted the title General Who Entices Righteousness, and was ennobled as a count.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 18 Ma Leiji was ordered to Guangxi to take charge of the armies; Ma Xiong was already dead, and his son Chengyin surrendered, was made General Who Entices Righteousness, and was ennobled a count.

sentences.zh: 已，部兵以餉匱譁，麻勒吉上言：「承廕與黃明、葉秉忠皆賊帥歸誠，今承廕授高爵，而明、秉忠未授官，故陰嗾兵士為變。

translations.literal: Later the troops mutinied from lack of rations; Ma Leiji stated: "Chengyin, together with Huang Ming and Ye Bingzhong, were all bandit chiefs who submitted in loyalty; now Chengyin has been granted a high rank while Ming and Bingzhong have not been given office, so they secretly incited the soldiers to mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the troops mutinied over unpaid rations; Ma Leiji reported: "Chengyin, Huang Ming, and Ye Bingzhong were all rebel chiefs who came over in good faith; Chengyin has been given a high title while Ming and Bingzhong have received no posts, and so they secretly stirred the soldiers to revolt.

sentences.zh: 秉忠年老無異志，惟明強悍，為柳州官兵所懾服，若不調用他所，終恐為害。」

translations.literal: Bingzhong is old and has no ulterior intent; only Ming is fierce and strong, and is feared and subdued by the officers and soldiers at Liuzhou; if he is not transferred elsewhere, in the end he will likely prove harmful."
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhong is old and loyal at heart; only Ming is fierce, and the Liuzhou garrison already fears him—unless he is posted elsewhere, he may yet do harm."

sentences.zh: 乃授明總兵官。

translations.literal: Thereupon Ming was granted the rank of regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: On that advice Ming was made regional commander.

sentences.zh: 明復叛，詔麻勒吉與偏沅巡撫韓世琦會剿，尋報為苗人所殺。

translations.literal: Ming rebelled again; an edict ordered Ma Leiji and Pianyuan Governor Han Shiqi to suppress him jointly, and soon a report came that he had been killed by Miao people.
translations.idiomatic: Ming rebelled again; Ma Leiji and Pianyuan Governor Han Shiqi were ordered to join forces against him, and word soon came that he had been killed by Miao tribesmen.

sentences.zh: 十九年，巡撫傅弘烈勦賊至柳州，承廕复叛，弘烈遇害，命麻勒吉兼攝巡撫事。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Governor Fu Honglie pursued bandits to Liuzhou; Chengyin rebelled again and Honglie was killed; Ma Leiji was ordered additionally to act as governor.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 19 Governor Fu Honglie pursued the rebels to Liuzhou; Chengyin rose again and Honglie was killed; Ma Leiji was ordered to act as governor as well.

sentences.zh: 時柳州再變，民多逃竄，田荒賦淆，麻勒吉招撫流亡，令歸故業，葺學宮，振興文教，頗著治績。

translations.literal: At the time Liuzhou had mutinied again; many people had fled, fields lay fallow, and tax records were confused; Ma Leiji enticed exiles back, ordered them to return to their former livelihoods, repaired the academy, revived culture and education, and achieved notable administrative results.
translations.idiomatic: Liuzhou was in turmoil again: people had fled, fields lay idle, and tax rolls were in chaos; Ma Leiji coaxed exiles home, restored their livelihoods, rebuilt the academy, and revived learning—with marked success.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，撤故定南王所部，分隸八旗漢軍，麻勒吉率以還京。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the troops formerly under the Prince of Dingnan were disbanded and assigned to the Eight Banners Han Army, and Ma Leiji led them back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 21 the old Prince of Dingnan's forces were broken up and assigned to the Han divisions of the Eight Banners, and Ma Leiji led them back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，授步軍統領。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was appointed Commander of the Metropolitan Infantry.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 23 he was made commander of the metropolitan infantry.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Kangxi 28.

sentences.zh: 三十七年，兵部奏黃明為貴州參將上官斌等所擒，麻勒吉追坐妄報。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh year the Ministry of War reported that Huang Ming had been captured by Guizhou Deputy General Shang Guanbin and others, and Ma Leiji was retrospectively punished for a false report.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 37 the Ministry of War reported that Huang Ming had been captured by Guizhou Deputy General Shang Guanbin and others, and Ma Leiji was posthumously faulted for his earlier false report.

sentences.zh: 奪官。

translations.literal: He was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: His office was revoked.

sentences.zh: 江南民為麻勒吉立碑雨花台紀績，祀名宦。

translations.literal: The people of Jiangnan erected a stele for Ma Leiji at Yuhuatai commemorating his achievements, and he was enshrined among notable officials.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan commoners raised a stele to him at Yuhuatai recording his deeds, and he was honored among notable officials.

sentences.zh: 阿席熙，瓜爾佳氏，滿洲鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Aixixi, of the Guwalgiya clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Aixixi, of the Guwalgiya clan, belonged to the Bordered Red Banner of the Manchu Eight Banners.

sentences.zh: 自兵部筆帖式四遷光祿寺卿。

translations.literal: From a clerk in the Board of War he was promoted four times to Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in four steps from a Board of War clerk to director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 考滿，輔政大臣鼇拜等令解任，隨旗行走，复坐事奪官。

translations.literal: When his performance review was complete, Regent Oboi and others ordered his removal from office and service according to banner assignment; he was again stripped of office for an offense.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of his term Regent Oboi and his colleagues dismissed him to banner duty, and he was later stripped of office again for another offense.

sentences.zh: 聖祖親政，鑑其無罪，命以郎中用。

translations.literal: When the Kangxi Emperor took personal rule, seeing that he was innocent, he ordered him appointed as a bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kangxi Emperor assumed personal rule and judged him innocent, he was restored as a bureau director.

sentences.zh: 七年，超擢陝西布政使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was exceptionally promoted to Shaanxi Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 7 he was abruptly promoted to Shaanxi provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 舉卓異，擢巡撫。

translations.literal: Recommended as outstanding, he was promoted to governor.
translations.idiomatic: Rated outstanding in evaluation, he was made governor.

sentences.zh: 康熙十二年，遷江南江西總督。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 12 he was transferred to Governor-General of Jiangnan and Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 12 he was transferred to governor-general of Jiangnan and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 耿精忠叛，窺江西，阿席熙發兵赴剿，並檄援浙江。

translations.literal: Geng Jingzhong rebelled and cast his eye on Jiangxi; Aixixi dispatched troops to suppress him and also issued orders to aid Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled and threatened Jiangxi, Aixixi sent troops against him and also ordered reinforcements for Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，精忠陷廣信、建昌、饒州，參將陳九傑等應之。

translations.literal: Before long Jingzhong captured Guangxin, Jianchang, and Raozhou, and Deputy General Chen Jiujie and others joined him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jingzhong took Guangxin, Jianchang, and Raozhou, and Deputy General Chen Jiujie and others went over to him.

sentences.zh: 阿席熙遣兵防徽州，賊陷績溪、婺源，擾及徽州，迭克之。

translations.literal: Aixixi sent troops to defend Huizhou; the bandits captured Jixi and Wuyuan, disturbed Huizhou as well, and he retook them in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Aixixi sent troops to guard Huizhou; rebels seized Jixi and Wuyuan and pressed Huizhou itself, but he recovered the towns one after another.

sentences.zh: 簡親王喇布率師至江寧，以阿席熙參贊軍務。

translations.literal: Prince Jian Labu led his army to Jiangning and appointed Aixixi to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Jian Labu marched to Jiangning, Aixixi was assigned to assist in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 十七年，疏報江南清出隱漏田地一萬四千餘頃、山八百餘裡，加兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he memorialized reporting that in Jiangnan more than fourteen thousand qing of hidden and omitted fields and more than eight hundred li of mountain land had been cleared, and he was promoted to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 17 he reported clearing more than fourteen thousand qing of concealed fields and over eight hundred li of unregistered mountain land in Jiangnan, and was promoted to minister of war.

sentences.zh: 尋坐瞻徇巡撫慕天顏奏銷浮冒，罷任。

translations.literal: Soon he was punished for indulging Governor Mu Tianyan's memorial of inflated expenses and was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon dismissed for covering for Governor Mu Tianyan's inflated expense accounts.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 阿席熙居官廉潔，江南士民德之，祀名宦。

translations.literal: Aixixi served with integrity and cleanliness; the gentry and people of Jiangnan honored him, and he was enshrined among notable officials.
translations.idiomatic: Aixixi served with scrupulous integrity; Jiangnan gentry and commoners held him in esteem, and he was honored among notable officials.

sentences.zh: 瑪祜，哲柏氏，滿洲鑲紅旗人。

translations.literal: Maku, of the Zhebo clan, was a Manchu of the Bordered Red Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Maku, of the Zhebo clan, belonged to the Bordered Red Banner of the Manchu Eight Banners.

sentences.zh: 順治九年繙譯進士。

translations.literal: In Shunzhi 9 he became a translation jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He took his translation jinshi degree in Shunzhi 9.

sentences.zh: 授佐領，兼刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed assistant commandant and concurrently served as Vice Director in the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was made an assistant commandant and concurrently a vice director in the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 遷欽天監監正。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Imperial Astronomical Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the Imperial Astronomical Bureau.

sentences.zh: 康熙八年，江寧巡撫缺，命議政大臣等會推滿洲郎中以上、學士以下通漢文有才能者備擢用，舉奏皆不當上意，特以命瑪祜。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 8, when the Jiangning governorship was vacant, regents and others were ordered jointly to recommend Manchu bureau directors and above through academicians and below who knew Chinese and had ability for elevation; the memorialized recommendations all failed to satisfy the emperor, and Maku was specially appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 8, with the Jiangning governorship vacant, the regents were told to nominate capable Manchu officials from bureau director up through academician who knew Chinese; none of their choices pleased the throne, and Maku was appointed by special order.

sentences.zh: 九年夏，淮安、揚州二府久雨，田廬多淹，詔發帑賑濟。

translations.literal: In the summer of the ninth year Huai'an and Yangzhou prefectures suffered prolonged rain, and many fields and dwellings were flooded; an edict ordered disbursement from the treasury for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Kangxi 9, long rains flooded fields and homes across Huai'an and Yangzhou, and the court ordered treasury relief.

sentences.zh: 瑪祜疏請蠲免桃源等縣積欠賦銀，及六、七兩年未完漕米，部議漕米無蠲免例，上特允其請，並蠲減蘇、松、常三府被災歲賦。

translations.literal: Maku memorialized requesting exemption of accumulated tax silver owed by Taoyuan and other counties and of unfinished grain transport from the sixth and seventh years; the Board deliberated that there was no precedent for exempting grain transport, but the emperor specially granted his request and also exempted and reduced the disaster-year taxes of the three prefectures of Suzhou, Songjiang, and Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Maku asked to write off accumulated tax silver in Taoyuan and other counties and unpaid grain transport from Kangxi 6 and 7; though the Board said grain transport had never been waived, the emperor granted his request and also cut disaster-year levies in Suzhou, Songjiang, and Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，疏言：「蘇、松二府額賦最重，由明洪武初以張士誠竊據其地，遷怒於民，取豪戶收租籍，付有司定賦額，較宋多七倍、元多三倍，是以民力困竭，積逋遂多。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he memorialized, saying: "The quota taxes of the two prefectures of Suzhou and Songjiang are the heaviest, because at the beginning of Ming Hongwu, when Zhang Shicheng seized that territory, anger was vented on the people: wealthy households' rent registers were taken and given to officials to fix the tax quota, which was seven times that of the Song and three times that of the Yuan; thus the people's strength was exhausted and accumulated arrears became numerous.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 10 he memorialized: "Suzhou and Songjiang bear the heaviest tax quotas because, at the start of Hongwu, the Ming punished the region for Zhang Shicheng's occupation by seizing wealthy landlords' rent rolls and fixing new quotas—seven times Song levels and three times Yuan—until the people were drained and arrears piled up.

sentences.zh: 自康熙元年至八年，民欠二百餘萬，催徵稍急，逃亡接踵，舊欠仍懸，新逋复積。

translations.literal: From Kangxi 1 to 8 the people owed more than two million; when collection was slightly urgent, flight followed in succession, old arrears still hung unpaid, and new arrears again accumulated.
translations.idiomatic: From Kangxi 1 through 8 the people owed more than two million taels; the harder collectors pressed, the more fled, old debts remained unpaid, and new ones mounted.

sentences.zh: 請敕部覈減二府浮糧，以期歲賦清完。」

translations.literal: He requested an edict to the Board to verify and reduce the inflated grain quotas of the two prefectures, in hope that the annual taxes might be cleared completely."
translations.idiomatic: He asked the throne to order the Board to review and cut the two prefectures' inflated quotas so annual levies could finally be cleared."

sentences.zh: 疏下部議，以科則久定，報寢。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the Board for deliberation; because the tax rates had long been fixed, the report was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the Board, which shelved it on the ground that tax rates had long been settled.

sentences.zh: 時布政使慕天顏請濬吳淞江、劉河，瑪祜與總督麻勒吉請以漕折十四萬充費。

translations.literal: At the time Provincial Administration Commissioner Mu Tianyan requested dredging the Wusong River and the Liuhe River; Maku together with Governor-General Ma Leiji requested that one hundred forty thousand taels of grain-transport conversion funds be used for expenses.
translations.idiomatic: When Provincial Administration Commissioner Mu Tianyan proposed dredging the Wusong River and Liuhe, Maku and Governor-General Ma Leiji asked that 140,000 taels of grain-transport conversion silver pay for the work.

sentences.zh: 給事中柯聳疏言，東南水利宜乘此興工，盡疏各支河。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Ke Song memorialized that southeast water conservancy ought to seize this opportunity to start work and fully dredge all branch rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Ke Song argued that the southeast waterworks should take this occasion to dredge every branch channel as well.

sentences.zh: 下瑪祜覆勘。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to Maku for reinvestigation.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Maku to reinvestigate.

sentences.zh: 瑪祜言各州縣支河皆已疏通，吳江縣長橋乃太湖洩水耍道，應令開濬。

translations.literal: Maku stated that branch rivers in the various prefectures and counties had all been cleared, but Changqiao in Wujiang County was a vital channel for discharging Taihu Lake and should be ordered opened and dredged.
translations.idiomatic: Maku reported that branch rivers throughout the prefectures were already clear, but Changqiao in Wujiang—the key outlet draining Taihu—still needed dredging.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以京口將軍李顯貴等侵餉事覺，坐不先舉發，罣吏議，當左遷，命留任。

translations.literal: Before long the embezzlement of rations by Jingkou General Li Xiangui and others came to light; Maku was punished for not having reported it first, was subject to disciplinary deliberation, and should have been demoted, but was ordered to remain in office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the embezzlement of rations by Jingkou General Li Xiangui and others came to light; faulted for not having exposed it, Maku faced demotion but was allowed to keep his post.

sentences.zh: 十二年，黃、淮水漲，清水潭石堤決，高郵等十八州縣衛所被災，瑪祜奏請發帑賑濟。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Yellow and Huai rivers rose, the stone embankment at Qingshuitan burst, and eighteen prefectures, counties, garrisons, and posts including Gaoyou were stricken; Maku memorialized requesting disbursement from the treasury for relief.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 12 floods on the Yellow and Huai burst the stone dike at Qingshuitan and devastated eighteen prefectures, counties, and garrisons including Gaoyou; Maku asked for treasury relief.

sentences.zh: 十五年，霪雨久不霽，以憂卒。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year prolonged rain long failed to clear, and he died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 15, after weeks of unbroken rain, he died of grief.

sentences.zh: 遺疏極陳水災民困，無一語及私。

translations.literal: His final memorial urgently set forth the flood disaster and the people's distress, without a single word concerning private matters.
translations.idiomatic: His death memorial spoke only of flood and suffering—not one word for himself.

sentences.zh: 詔褒惜，諡清恪。

translations.literal: An edict praised and mourned him, and he was posthumously titled Qingke.
translations.idiomatic: The throne mourned him with praise and gave him the posthumous title Qingke, Pure and Respectful.

sentences.zh: 施維翰，字及甫，江南華亭人。

translations.literal: Shi Weihan, courtesy name Jifu, was a native of Huating in Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Weihan, styled Jifu, came from Huating in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 順治九年進士，授江西臨江推官，清漕弊，善折獄，姦頑斂跡。

translations.literal: A jinshi of Shunzhi 9, he was appointed River-Defense Judge of Linjiang in Jiangxi, cleared abuses in grain transport, was skilled at deciding cases, and scoundrels restrained their steps.
translations.idiomatic: A Shunzhi 9 jinshi, he served as river-defense judge of Linjiang in Jiangxi, cleaned up grain-transport abuses, judged cases with skill, and made rogues mend their ways.

sentences.zh: 巡撫郎廷佐奏其治行，舉卓異，內擢兵部主事。

translations.literal: Governor Lang Tingzuo memorialized his administrative conduct, recommended him as outstanding, and he was promoted internally to Principal Clerk in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Lang Tingzuo reported his record, rated him outstanding, and he was brought to the capital as a principal clerk in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 改山東道御史，疏言：「察吏首重懲貪，尤宜先嚴大吏。

translations.literal: Transferred to censor of the Shandong circuit, he memorialized, saying: "In inspecting officials, punishing corruption comes first, and it is especially fitting to be strict with great officials first.
translations.idiomatic: Made censor of the Shandong circuit, he memorialized: "In inspecting officials, punishing graft must come first—and senior officials above all.

sentences.zh: 各督撫按露章彈劾，宜及監司，勿僅以州縣塞責。」

translations.literal: When each governor-general, governor, and provincial censor openly memorializes impeachments, they should reach the surveillance and administration commissioners and not merely use prefectures and counties to fulfill responsibility."
translations.idiomatic: When governors-general, governors, and provincial censors impeach by open memorial, they should reach the surveillance commissioners—not stop at county and prefectural officials to satisfy form."

sentences.zh: 又言；

translations.literal: He also stated:
translations.idiomatic: He also said:

sentences.zh: 「糾舉之法，密於文，疏於武。

translations.literal: "The method of impeachment is strict for civil officials and lax for military officers.
translations.idiomatic: "Impeachment is tight for civil officials and loose for military commanders.

sentences.zh: 鎮帥擁重兵，有庸碌衰憊、緩急難恃者，有縱恣婪贓、肆虐軍民者，督撫按徇隱弗糾，事發同罪。」

translations.literal: Regional commanders hold heavy troops; some are mediocre, decrepit, and unreliable in crisis, and some indulge themselves in greedy corruption and tyrannize army and people alike; if governors-general, governors, and censors indulge and conceal and do not impeach, when the matter breaks out they share the guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Regional commanders wield great armies—some are dull, worn out, and useless in a crisis; others plunder freely and terrorize soldiers and civilians alike. If governors and censors cover for them and fail to impeach, they share guilt when scandal breaks."

sentences.zh: 詔並議行。

translations.literal: An edict ordered both proposals deliberated and implemented.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered both proposals adopted.

sentences.zh: 十七年，出按陝西。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he went out to inspect Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 17 he was sent to inspect Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 聖祖即位，裁巡按，維翰乞假歸。

translations.literal: When the Kangxi Emperor ascended the throne, touring censors were abolished, and Weihan requested leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kangxi Emperor took the throne and touring censors were abolished, Weihan asked leave to go home.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，复授江南道御史，疏言：「直省錢糧，每委府佐協徵，所至鋪設供給，不免擾民。

translations.literal: In Kangxi 3 he was again appointed censor of the Jiangnan circuit and memorialized, saying: "In the provinces, funds and grain are often entrusted to prefectural assistants to collect jointly; wherever they go, furnishings and supplies are laid out, and the people cannot avoid being harassed.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 3 he was again made censor of the Jiangnan circuit and memorialized: "Provincial tax collection is often delegated to prefectural deputies, whose retinues and provisioning wherever they go inevitably harass the people.

sentences.zh: 甚或縱容胥役，橫肆誅求。

translations.literal: Some even indulged clerks and runners to extort wildly and demand arbitrarily.
translations.idiomatic: Some even let clerks and runners run wild with extortion and arbitrary levies.

sentences.zh: 請概行禁止，以專責成、杜擾害。」

translations.literal: I request a general prohibition, to fix responsibility and stop harassment."
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a general ban to fix responsibility and end the abuse."

sentences.zh: 下部飭禁。

translations.literal: The ministries were ordered to forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: The ministries were ordered to enforce the ban.

sentences.zh: 巡鹽河東，徵課如額。

translations.literal: He toured salt administration in Hedong and collected tax to quota.
translations.idiomatic: Touring Hedong salt administration, he collected the full quota.

sentences.zh: 八年，疏劾偏沅巡撫周召南徇庇貪吏。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he memorialized impeaching Pianyuan Governor Zhou Zhaonan for shielding greedy officials.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 8 he impeached Pianyuan Governor Zhou Zhaonan for shielding corrupt officials.

sentences.zh: 十一年，疏劾福建總督劉鬥徇情題建故靖南王耿繼茂祠。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he memorialized impeaching Fujian Governor-General Liu Dou for partiality in proposing a shrine to the late Prince Jingnan Geng Jimao.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 11 he impeached Fujian Governor-General Liu Dou for favoritism in proposing a shrine to the late Prince Jingnan Geng Jimao.

sentences.zh: 召南、鬥並坐譴。

translations.literal: Zhaonan and Dou were both punished by reprimand.
translations.idiomatic: Both Zhaonan and Dou were reprimanded.

sentences.zh: 十二年，內升，以四品服俸仍留御史任。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was promoted internally, given fourth-rank salary and robes while remaining in his censor post.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 12 he was promoted within the censorate, given fourth-rank pay while keeping his post.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「設登聞鼓，原以伸士民冤抑，故使科道共與其事。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The grievance drum was established originally to give gentry and commoners voice for wrongs suppressed; therefore censors were made to share in the matter.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "The grievance drum was meant to give scholars and commoners a voice; censors were therefore assigned to hear petitions.

sentences.zh: 然每收訴狀，必待科道六十餘員集議，輒致稽延。

translations.literal: Yet whenever a petition is received, more than sixty censors must assemble for deliberation, which always causes delay.
translations.idiomatic: Yet every petition waits for sixty-odd censors to meet, which only causes delay.

sentences.zh: 請用滿、漢科道各一員司之，半年更易。」

translations.literal: I request that one Manchu and one Han censor manage it, rotated every half year."
translations.idiomatic: Let one Manchu and one Han censor handle it, rotating every six months."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 遷鴻臚寺少卿，累遷左副都御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and was repeatedly promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He became vice minister of the Court of State Ceremonial and rose to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 浙江巡撫陳秉直薦舉學道陳汝璞，為左都御史魏象樞所劾，秉直應降調，以加級抵銷。

translations.literal: Zhejiang Governor Chen Bingzhi recommended Education Commissioner Chen Rupu; Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Xiangshu impeached him; Bingzhi should have been demoted and transferred, but offset his penalty with a rank increase.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang Governor Chen Bingzhi recommended Education Commissioner Chen Rupu; Left Censor-in-Chief Wei Xiangshu impeached the nomination; Bingzhi should have been demoted but offset it with a rank increase.

sentences.zh: 維翰言：「秉直與汝璞見聞最近，乃徇情妄舉，非尋常詿誤可比。

translations.literal: Weihan said: "Bingzhi and Rupu were in closest contact; this was partiality in a reckless recommendation, not comparable to ordinary error.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan argued: "Bingzhi knew Rupu well—this was favoritism, not an ordinary mistake.

sentences.zh: 請敕部定議，凡保舉非人坐降調者，不許抵銷。」

translations.literal: I request an edict to the ministries to fix the rule: whoever recommends an unfit person and is sentenced to demotion and transfer may not offset the penalty."
translations.idiomatic: He asked the ministries to rule that wrongful recommendations punished by demotion may not be offset by rank increases."

sentences.zh: 上然之，因著為列。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and made it a standing regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and made it permanent law.

sentences.zh: 給事中李宗孔繼劾秉直，坐左遷。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Li Zongkong impeached Bingzhi again; he was sentenced to demotion and transfer.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Li Zongkong impeached Bingzhi again, and he was demoted.

sentences.zh: 十八年，授山東巡撫。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he was appointed provincial governor of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 18 he was made provincial governor of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 會歲祲，民多流亡，維翰疏請賑恤，並截留漕米五萬石發濟南倉存貯，散給饑民。

translations.literal: A famine year came; many people fled; Weihan memorialized requesting relief, and also detained fifty thousand shi of grain-transport rice to store in the Jinan granary and distribute to the hungry.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck and people fled, Weihan asked for relief, detained fifty thousand shi of transport grain for the Jinan granary, and fed the hungry.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「青、萊等府距臨清倉遠，辦解甚艱。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "The prefectures of Qing and Lai and others are far from the Linqing granary, and delivery is very hard.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Qing, Lai, and other prefectures lie far from the Linqing granary, and delivery is arduous.

sentences.zh: 請永行改折，以息轉輸。」

translations.literal: I request permanent commutation to silver payments, to end long-distance transport."
translations.idiomatic: He asked for permanent commutation to silver to end the long haul."

sentences.zh: 民大悅服。

translations.literal: The people were greatly pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The people were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，代李之芳為浙江總督。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he replaced Li Zhifang as governor-general of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 21 he replaced Li Zhifang as governor-general of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 之芳按治軍士鼓譟，系累二百餘人。

translations.literal: Zhifang had investigated soldiers who mutinied with drum clamor and detained more than two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang had investigated a soldiers' mutiny and held more than two hundred men.

sentences.zh: 維翰至，即日定讞，多平反。

translations.literal: When Weihan arrived, he settled the cases that same day and reversed many verdicts.
translations.idiomatic: Weihan arrived, settled the cases the same day, and reversed many convictions.

sentences.zh: 二十二年冬，調福建，未上官，二十三年春，卒，諡清惠。

translations.literal: In the winter of the twenty-second year he was transferred to Fujian but before taking office, in the spring of the twenty-third year he died; posthumous title Qinghui.
translations.idiomatic: In winter Kangxi 22 he was transferred to Fujian; before taking office he died in spring Kangxi 23; posthumous title Qinghui.

sentences.zh: 論曰：李率泰鎮福建，禦鄭成功父子，趙廷臣督浙江，執張煌言，有功於戡定。

translations.literal: The historians comment: Li Lvtai governed Fujian and resisted Zheng Chenggong father and son; Zhao Tingchen governed Zhejiang and captured Zhang Huangyan—they had merit in pacification.
translations.idiomatic: The historians write: Li Lvtai held Fujian against Zheng Chenggong and his son; Zhao Tingchen governed Zhejiang and captured Zhang Huangyan—both served the pacification.

sentences.zh: 郎廷佐釐逋賦。

translations.literal: Lang Tingzuo straightened out tax arrears.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Tingzuo sorted out tax arrears.

sentences.zh: 佟鳳彩均里甲、蠲夫柳，為民袪害。

translations.literal: Tong Fengcai equalized li and jia and exempted labor and willows, removing harm for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Fengcai reformed lijia and relieved labor and willow levies, lifting burdens from the people.

sentences.zh: 麻勒吉初奉使迫張玄錫至死，聖祖諭斥其縱恣。

translations.literal: Ma Leiji on an early mission drove Zhang Xuanxi to attempt death; the Shizu Emperor rebuked his arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Leiji's early mission drove Zhang Xuanxi to suicide; the Shizu Emperor rebuked his arrogance.

sentences.zh: 然於江南有惠政，阿席熙、瑪祜清望尤過之。

translations.literal: Yet in Jiangnan he had benevolent policies; Aixixi and Maku's reputations for integrity surpassed him even more.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he left benevolent rule in Jiangnan; Aixixi and Maku's reputations for integrity stood even higher.

sentences.zh: 施維翰在台敢言，出持疆節，措置得大體。

translations.literal: Shi Weihan at the censorate spoke boldly; going out to hold a frontier commission, his arrangements grasped the larger pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Weihan spoke boldly as a censor; as a frontier governor his measures were sound in the large.

sentences.zh: 皆康熙初賢大吏也。

translations.literal: All were worthy great officials of early Kangxi.
translations.idiomatic: All were worthy high officials of early Kangxi.

sentences.zh: 愷悌君子，屏籓王國，厥績懋矣！

translations.literal: Kind and harmonious gentlemen, screens and bulwarks of the realm—their achievements were abundant!
translations.idiomatic: Benevolent gentlemen, bulwarks of the realm—their achievements were great indeed!
